meta.note: Machine-assisted translation of the Chinese taxonomic prose in _data/*.json. Latin names, authorities, years and measurements are kept verbatim; the pre-existing English abstracts in the source `en` fields are not duplicated here.

/genus/acanthotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 13–14). Type species of the genus: Acanthotermes acanthothorax (Sjöstedt). The species list (7 African species) is not included in the description. Note: the dimorphic soldier is the older view of Holmgren 1912 (who described only large and small forms); the keys to Macrotermitinae in Grassé 1937 and Treatise 2013 distinguish a medium soldier as well, and the soldiers of this genus are now regarded as large, medium and small.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldiers are of three sizes — large, medium and small — which is the most conspicuous character of the genus; alate antennae 20–23-segmented, the male with 1–2 more segments than the female, soldier antennae 17–20-segmented. Anterior margin of the pronotum with spines, lateral margins of the thoracic tergites more or less acute. All known species are from Africa.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broad, nearly circular. Compound eyes medium-sized and protruding; ocelli directed slightly laterally, nearly circular, about one eye diameter from the compound eyes. Frontal gland opening present. Base of the clypeus even longer than half its width, rather narrow, posterior margin strongly convex, anterior margin straight, considerably raised, distinctly brighter than the frons; distal part of the clypeus transparent. Labrum longer than wide, with a chitinous transverse band. Mandibles with the Termes-type dentition, the first tooth of the left mandible slightly larger than the second. Pronotum with two small tuberculate projections on each side of the midline. Posterior notch of the mesonotum slightly wider than that of the metanotum. Wings transparent, with brown veins at the base and along the anterior margin, membrane weakly reticulate; radius reduced, not extending beyond the wing scale; media of the forewing separate from the wing scale, media of the hindwing arising from the base of the radial sector, slender, branching towards the radial sector and the wing apex; cubitus with a thickened inner vein. Sides of the abdomen with exudatory setae, denser in the female; male with styli.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Major soldier: head narrowing more or less anteriorly, sides parallel, oval to cordate, posterior margin straight to strongly concave. Frontal gland opening distinct, surrounded by a circular area bearing setae, with a spine-like projection in front of the opening; base of the mandibles stout. Base of the clypeus very short, distal part rather large and transparent. Labrum rather wide, distal part trilobed and transparent. Mandibles rather short and stout, more or less strongly curved, each with a more or less sharp large basal tooth; left mandible with an additional 3 to several rather small tuberculate teeth, its base often notched and projecting as a tooth; rest of the right mandible toothless. Postmentum long, narrow, parallel-sided. Anterior margin of the pronotum with two pointed projections on each side of the midline, rather small, anterolateral angles rather sharp; lateral parts of mesonotum and metanotum more or less acute. Legs long, the last tarsomere distinctly longer than the remaining tarsomeres together, slender. Cerci large; styli present but small, or reduced.
Minor soldier: head rather parallel-sided, oval, widest at the level of the antennae; in lateral view both upper and lower surfaces rather convex, the lower especially wrinkled. The frontal gland opening is likewise surrounded by a ring of setae, sometimes raised into a tube, with a distinct spine on its anterior margin. Clypeus rather short, posterior margin convex, anterior margin straight, with a transparent distal part. Labrum pointed, distal part transparent and trilobed. Mandibles narrow, weakly sickle-shaped, the base of the left mandible with tooth marks, the basal tooth weakly developed. Antennae long, 15–20-segmented, segment 2 shorter than segment 3. Postmentum elongate, strongly convex, narrow and parallel-sided. Anterior margin of the pronotum with spines. Cerci large; styli present.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Two forms. Head large, broadly oval, coronal suture distinct, frontal gland opening large and triangular. Base of the clypeus short, much shorter than half its width, raised, distal part large. Labrum longer than wide, with a chitinous transverse band. Mandibles shorter and wider than in the alate, but with the same dentition. Antennae 17–21-segmented, segment 2 longer than segment 3. Pronotum with stout anterior projections. Legs long, foretrochanter with two stout anterior setae. Cerci large; styli reduced.

/genus/acorhinotermes/.note: The original has no separate genus-level Diagnosis section; the generic characters are taken from the generic history in the Introduction and from the first couplet of the subfamily key based on the minor soldier; the rest is the species-level description of A. claritae, marked as species level at each point. The only copy available locally is the publisher's JATS XML (Europe PMC PMC6882922), with no print PDF, so the locator uses section names. An alate is illustrated only for A. subfusciceps, and no alate section was written from it here.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The diagnostic character at generic level is the absence of a major soldier, the feature on which Emerson based the removal of the species from Rhinotermes and the erection of this genus; in dorsal view the fontanelle of the minor soldier lies in front of the mandibular lobes (that is, the bases of the mandibular points), which separates it from Dolichorhinotermes and Rhinotermes, in both of which the fontanelle lies at or behind the mandibular lobes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Only the minor soldier is known. In dorsal view the sides of the head are concave, producing a posterior constriction; the vertex bears 10–12 long, erect setae and no microtrichia; antennae 15 or 16 segments, with the formula 2=3<4=5; mandibles reduced, long, straight and sharp; labrum extremely long (hyperelongate), widening towards the apex, which is bilobed, and in lateral view almost in the same plane as the vertex; fontanelle situated at 1/5 of the length from the base of the labrum; pronotum concolorous with the head, bearing 4–8 scattered setae (2–4 on the anterior margin and 2–4 on the dorsum) and no microtrichia; abdominal segments pale yellow, densely hairy at the margins; legs with numerous long and short setae, the fore tibia with stout setae. The mandibular points of the minor soldier of this species are longer than in A. subfusciceps, and the body is relatively smaller.

/genus/acutidentitermes/.note: Of the type species only the soldier and worker are known; the original does not describe the alate. Rewritten from the English genus diagnosis, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to Hoplognathotermes but distinguishable in the soldier: head very large, sides slightly convex and nearly parallel; postmentum more bulbous, its lateral margins overlapping and concealing the lateral suture; suture between postclypeus and frons far less distinct; labrum with sharper lateral and median points; anteriorly directed mandibular teeth longer, sharper and more anteriorly directed; anterior lobe of the pronotum larger and longer, the median notch of the anterior margin deeper and wider; fore femur relatively long and slender. Alate unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head surface with only a few rather short setae, none near the fontanelle; postmentum completely hairless, without setae; first 4 abdominal tergites with rather long setae, almost without short hairs, posterior tergites and sternites with additional short hairs. Head very large, sides slightly convex and nearly parallel, fontanelle small. Postmentum more bulbous than in Hoplognathotermes, its posterior lateral margins overlapping, so that in ventral view the outer suture is concealed except near the posterior margin; posterior part of the postmentum without a transverse ridge. Antennae 15-segmented. Suture between postclypeus and frons far less distinct than in Hoplognathotermes. Labrum with sharper lateral and median points. Both mandibles with conspicuous anteriorly directed teeth, but longer, sharper and more anteriorly directed than in Hoplognathotermes; apical outward curvature weaker; the notch on the side at the boundary between apex and base less conspicuous. Anterior lobe of the pronotum larger and longer than in Hoplognathotermes, the median notch of the anterior margin more conspicuous and wider, the posterior margin more concave. Fore coxa simple, the longitudinal ridge obtuse, moderately sharp, straight or slightly convex in section, without coarse spines; fore femur relatively long and slender. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Differs from Hoplognathotermes as follows: the angle between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth of both mandibles is sharper; the cutting edges of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible are proportionally slightly longer; the upper ridge of the molar region of the right mandible is sharper and more concave.

/genus/allognathotermes/.note: In the full text available locally (Emerson 1956) this genus has only species-level descriptions and a discussion of its systematic position, with no separate genus-level morphological account; Emerson 1959 also does not treat the genus separately, its generic characters occurring scattered in comparative sentences within the generic characters of Duplidentitermes. Hence only those genus-level comparative features that explicitly concern Allognathotermes are included here, without supplementation or extrapolation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to Hoplognathotermes and Duplidentitermes. The mandibular teeth of the soldier are less conspicuous than in those two, but the left mandible has 2 rather widely separated teeth, apparently homologous with the bidentate teeth of Duplidentitermes; the fore coxal ridge is very similar to that of Duplidentitermes, only slightly more evident because it extends with a slight inward curve; the fore femur is short and stout, as in Duplidentitermes, and clearly different from the slender fore femur of Firmitermes, Hoplognathotermes and Acutidentitermes. The second marginal tooth of the right mandible of the alate is reduced to a small mound.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The second marginal tooth of the right mandible is reduced to a small mound, as in Duplidentitermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The mandibular teeth are less conspicuous than in Hoplognathotermes and Duplidentitermes, but the left mandible has 2 rather widely separated teeth, apparently homologous with the bidentate teeth of the left mandible of Duplidentitermes. The longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa is very similar to that of Duplidentitermes, only slightly more evident owing to a slightly curved inward extension. The fore femur is short and stout, as in Duplidentitermes, whereas in Firmitermes, Hoplognathotermes and Acutidentitermes it is slender.

/genus/anoplotermes/.note: The original explicitly records that soldiers are entirely absent, hence this genus has only the alate and worker sections. This is a Neotropical genus; the African "Anoplotermes" has been separated out, so the African literature (Sands 1972) does not contain the generic characters of this genus.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldiers entirely absent. Alate head very broad, usually densely hairy, compound eyes small and prominent, the fontanelle situated far back or at the middle of the head; antennae constantly 15-segmented, segment 3 much shorter; wings dark, hairy and spinose; tibiae with 2 apical spurs. Worker similar to the worker of Eutermes, postclypeus strongly arched, antennae constantly 14-segmented, head mostly pale, fontanelle indistinct.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head very broad, usually densely hairy, compound eyes small and prominent; fontanelle either far back or at the middle of the head; ocelli medium-sized, their distance from the compound eyes variable; basal piece of the postclypeus almost always at least half as long as its width (except A. iheringi), usually strongly arched; transverse band longer in the middle than at the sides; mandibles with 1 large apical tooth, slightly elongate; antennae constantly 15-segmented, segment 3 usually far shorter than the adjacent segments; brain large. Pronotum as in Eutermes; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum more or less deeply concave; wings dark, hairy and spinose, venation as in Eutermes; tibiae with 2 apical spurs; abdomen elongate, the sides of the female with glandular hairs.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Similar to the worker of Eutermes; postclypeus strongly arched, as long as or even longer than half its width; antennae constantly 14-segmented, segment 3 mostly shorter than the adjacent segments; head mostly pale, fontanelle indistinct.

/genus/apicotermes/.note: The original has only the wings of the alate available for description ("Imago: Nur die Flügel sind vorhanden"), so no head or body characters could be recorded. Emerson (1959: 26), in a comparison, separately records that in this genus the setae at the anterior end of the soldier labrum are clustered, which adds one further character.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Of the alate the original makes known only the wings: in the forewing the area between the costa and the radial sector is unusually broad at the base, the radial vein very well developed and giving off 1–2 anterior branches, the media with 6–8 branches, the cubitus with about 14 closely set branches. Soldier head elongate, rectangular, about 1.5 times as long as wide, frons flat and slightly triangularly depressed, fontanelle small, distinct, surrounded by no hairs; mandibles short and very robust; antennae 14-segmented; fore coxa with an anteriorly directed tooth-like process. Worker head very broad, subcircular, pale, basal piece of the postclypeus very large and strongly arched, antennae 15-segmented, fore coxa with a large tooth-like process.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Forewing: the area between the costa and the radial sector is unusually broad at the base; within this area the radial vein is unusually well developed and even gives off 1–2 anterior branches running towards the costa; the base of the radial sector sometimes bears 1 short anterior vein and has a distal posterior branch; the media arises independently from the wing scale and has 6–8 branches; the cubitus has about 14 closely set branches, all reaching the posterior margin of the wing, of which the inner 8–9 are partly concealed; the area between the radial sector and the media is distinctly reticulate. Hindwing: the radial vein is shorter than in the forewing; the media has a thicker anterior accessory vein in the inner 1/3 and gives off 4–5 branches towards the wing apex or the posterior margin; the cubitus has about 16 posterior branches; the rest as in the forewing. Wing surface, especially at the base, dark, finely punctate; forewing 12.5 mm long.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head elongate, rectangular, about 1.5 times as long as wide, narrowing only very slightly anteriorly, relatively flat; frons flat, slightly triangularly depressed; fontanelle small but distinct, surrounded by no hairs. Basal piece of the postclypeus not sharply delimited from the frons, the apical piece smaller. Labrum relatively broad, ligulate, with a short, rounded, white, hairy apex. Mandibles short and very robust, the apices curving inwards rather strongly; the left mandible with 3 tooth-like swellings at the apex and in the middle, the outermost largest, situated about the middle of the apical half of the mandible; base large, with a strong basal swelling; the right mandible with 2 weak tooth-like swellings in the middle, the molar angle short and small, with 1 small anteriorly directed rudimentary tooth on the base behind it. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 about half of segment 2, segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 2. Pronotum pale yellow and sclerotised, narrower than the head, shallowly saddle-shaped, anterior lobe large, anterior and posterior margins slightly concave. Dark intestinal contents visible through the abdomen; cerci short, without stylus; fore coxa with an anteriorly directed tooth-like process.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head (very) broad, subcircular, pale; fontanelle plate about at the middle of the head; basal piece of the postclypeus very large, very strongly arched, as long as half its width; first mandibular tooth larger than the second but not large; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 short; anterior lobe of the pronotum very large, saddle-shaped; cerci small, without stylus.

/genus/apilitermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, p. 103). The alate section is marked 'unbekannt' in the original, so no 'Alate' section is given; a 'Nymph' section is provided on the basis of the nymph material alone. The worker section in the original consists of a single comparative sentence and is not expanded; this is stated in the text rather than reproducing the provisions for Crenetermes. The Chinese generic name is undetermined (marked '—' in the batch), so the Latin name is used provisionally.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A new genus established by Holmgren 1912, with the single species Apilitermes longiceps (Sjöst.) from Cameroon; a synonym in part of Eutermes (Sjöstedt) and in part of Termes (Desneux). The alate is unknown and is inferred only from the nymph. The soldier head is long rectangular, the frontal gland opening lying behind the inclined frontal surface on the horizontal part of the head, without surrounding hairs, with a fine groove running forward from the frontal gland opening; the labrum is quadrangular and grooved, with a non-concave anterior margin; the mandibles are long and straight, the apex and the middle continuous as one piece, with a small tooth-like, step-like swelling at the base; antennae of 15 segments. For the worker the original text records only 'the same as Crenetermes'.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long rectangular, fairly convex, anterior margin obliquely truncate. Frontal gland opening behind the posterior edge of the inclined frontal surface, on the horizontal part of the head, small, without surrounding hairs; a fine groove extends forward from it. Clypeus flat, the base small, the clypeal apical piece large. Labrum quadrangular, widening anteriorly, grooved, the anterior margin not concave. Mandibles long, robust and straight, slightly curved towards the apex; dentition as in Crenetermes, but the base of the right mandible smaller; apex and middle joined as one unit, with a separate small tooth-like, step-like swelling at its base, sharply delimited from the base; the apex and middle of the left mandible in particular are finely serrate. Antennae of 15 segments, segment 3 short. Pronotum small, strongly saddle-shaped. Without styli.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The original text gives only one comparative sentence: the same as the worker of Crenetermes (»Wie bei Crenetermes.«), without listing further characters, so the provisions for Crenetermes are not reproduced here.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: Male nymph with degenerate styli (the original places this under the alate heading; because the adult is unknown, it is judged from the nymph).

/genus/archotermopsis/.note: When the original was published the genus was named Termopsis (Heer); the passage on generic characters actually covers the then broad sense of Termopsis (including what is now Zootermopsis); on p. 297 the author states that he had already erected the subgenus Archotermopsis (Desneux 1904, Genera Insectorum XXV, p. 18), and the type species described in the paper is A. wroughtoni, so the generic characters and the species-level description can be assigned to this genus, but it should be noted that some of the features in the generic characters may belong to Termopsis in the broad sense. The generic characters give 27–28 antennal segments, whereas the species-level description gives 24 or 25; the two are inconsistent and must be checked before use.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original gives the generic characters under the name Termopsis: the alate lacks ocelli entirely and the frontal plate is not projecting, which separates it from groups possessing ocelli; the tarsi appear 4-segmented but are actually 5-segmented, segment 2 being only partly separated from segment 1, and a plantula is present between the tarsal claws; the cerci are long and the male styli are well developed; the wings are broad, less than 4 times as long as wide. The soldier is robust, with a large, subrectangular and flattened head, antennae of more than 20 segments, very strong mandibles with teeth on the inner margin, a pronotum narrower than the head and nearly flat, and long cerci and styli. The author subsequently erected the subgenus Archotermopsis on features such as the shape of the compound eye and the remnants of the wing bases, and noted that it differs from the remaining members of Termopsis.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Antennae 27–28 segments (the species-level description of the type species, A. wroughtoni, gives 24 or 25 segments, which conflicts with the generic characters and must be checked against specimens); ocelli entirely absent; frontal plate not projecting; compound eyes large, the anterior margin deeply incised and almost kidney-shaped (species level); pronotum nearly flat and narrower than the head; wings less than 4 times as long as wide, the forewing with a subcosta, the radius well developed and giving off several branches that reach the anterior margin, the media near the middle of the wing, the membranous area densely reticulate; tibiae with lateral spines; tarsi appearing 4-segmented but actually 5-segmented, with a plantula between the claws; cerci long and male styli well developed.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body robust; head large, subrectangular and flattened, the posterior margin distinctly concave (species level); eyes small or reduced, the species-level description recording them as small, oval and without ommatidia; antennae of more than 20 segments (species level 22–25 segments); mandibles very strong, the inner margin with irregular strong teeth, the apices curved inwards and sharp; pronotum narrower than the head and nearly flat; tarsi without a plantula (the original states that the plantula occurs only in the alate); cerci and styli both long.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The original (the species-level description of A. wroughtoni) states that the worker resembles a larva: in the nymphal type the meso- and metathoracic epimera form triangular, leaf-like free processes, as in the soldier, whereas the alate lacks such processes; in some individuals the posterior margins of the meso- and metanota retain scars from broken wing buds, and the head is slightly larger than in the nymph; the original suggests that such individuals perform the worker function.

/genus/armitermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 53–54). Armitermes in the original includes the three subgenera Armitermes s. str., Curvitermes and Rhynchotermes, the generic characters being common to all three; the 5 forms of mid-mandibular tooth arrangement in the soldier (numbered 1–5 in the original) have not been translated one by one.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate differs very little from that of Cornitermes, only in the head and body being on average slightly smaller, antennae 14–15 segments; the soldier head is pyriform, drawn anteriorly into a short or long conical frontal tube, the frontal gland opening lies at the apex of the tube, the frontal gland is very large, antennae 13–14 segments, the pronotum is more saddle-shaped than in Cornitermes and the anterior lobe is often shorter. Worker pale, head small. Holmgren 1912 divided the genus into three subgenera, Armitermes s. str., Curvitermes and Rhynchotermes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Differs very little from the alate of Cornitermes, the head on average smaller and the body also slightly smaller. Compound eyes variable in size; ocelli variable in size and position. Frontal gland opening distinct, small to very large; frons slightly depressed. Base of clypeus strongly arched, as long as or longer than half its width, brighter than the frons, posterior margin strongly convex, anterior margin straight. Mandibular first tooth larger than the second or equal to it, in which case the antennae have 14 segments; antennae 14–15 segments, in the former case the third segment much longer than the remaining ones, in the latter shorter than the second. Thorax and wings as in Cornitermes, but the first cubital branch of the wing distinctly stouter than the subsequent ones; wing membrane sometimes weakly punctate.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pyriform, drawn anteriorly into a short or long conical frontal tube; frontal gland opening large, at the apex of the frontal tube, frontal gland very large. Transverse band and frons both very small, hidden beneath the 'nose'. Clypeus small, almost indistinguishable from the transverse band. Labrum short and relatively broad. Mandibles often very strongly curved; left base large to very large, often with a sharp molar angle, or with 2 sharp teeth before the molar angle; the middle tooth arrangement is variable, the original describing the number of teeth, their separation or fusion, and the shape of the molar angle in 5 forms. Antennae 13–14 segments. Pronotum usually more saddle-shaped than in Cornitermes, anterior lobe often shorter, otherwise as in that genus.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Pale. Head small, concolorous with the rest of the body, more or less pentagonal and rounded. Base of clypeus about as long as half its width, strongly arched, posterior margin strongly convex, anterior margin straight and sharply defined. Mandibular first tooth almost always longer than the second. Antennae 14–15 segments. Pronotum as in the soldier.

/genus/capritermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 114–116). In 1912 the genus contained two subgenera (Neocapritermes, Capritermes s. str.), and what is described here are the combined characters at generic level; the lists of subgenera and species are on pp. 115–116 (Old World species: chiasognathus, socialis, capricornis, ceylonicus, foraminifer, incola, medius, minor, nemorosus, etc.). zh_name provisionally uses the Latin name (marked '—' in the batch).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Holmgren 1912 divided the genus into two clearly delimited subgenera: Neocapritermes (all the American species, plus the African C. alienus v. Rosen) and Capritermes s. str. (Old World species only). The key differences between the two are: in the alate, the size of the first and second teeth, the number of antennal segments, the shape of the posterior margins of meso- and metanotum, and the presence or absence of a radius in the forewing; in the soldier, only the presence or absence of the frontal gland opening — Neocapritermes lacks it, Capritermes s. str. has it; in the worker, whether the anterior margin of the fore coxa is slightly disc-like expanded and the size of the first tooth. Characters common to the genus are: alate antennae 15–17 segments, third segment mostly short, wing membrane dark with spine-like points, media close to the cubitus; soldier head elongate rectangular, flattened and arched, mandibles of Capritermes type, asymmetrically curved, antennae 13–16 segments; worker head more or less pentagonal and rounded, antennae 13–15 segments.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, narrowing anteriorly. Compound eyes relatively small, mostly strongly projecting. Ocelli variable in position, facing laterally. Frontal gland opening depressed. Base of clypeus flatly convex, shorter than half its width. Mandibles in two conditions: either with a large apical tooth (in which case the posterior part of meso- and metanotum is pointed, antennae (14–)15 segments); or with the first two teeth about equal in length (in which case the posterior part of meso- and metanotum is broad, the mesonotum hardly incised, the metanotum broadly incised, antennae 17 segments and the forewing with a radius). Antennae 15–17 segments, third segment mostly short. Wing membrane dark, with small points (spines). Media close to the cubitus. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with 2 each.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head slender rectangular, rarely narrowing anteriorly, flattened and arched. Frontal gland opening mostly present, exposed on the front of the head; absent in all the American species and in the African C. alienus. Base of clypeus very narrow. Labrum slender: either with the lateral angles projecting and the middle rounded or incised, or trilobed with the lobes very short and rounded. Mandibles of Capritermes type, asymmetrically curved. Antennae 13–16 segments. Pronotum small, saddle-shaped.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head more or less pentagonal and rounded. Base of clypeus strongly arched, slightly shorter than half its width. Shape of the mandibular first tooth as in the alate. Antennae 13–15 segments. Pronotum saddle-shaped.

/genus/caputitermes/.note: There is no soldier section (Neotropical Apicotermitinae lack soldiers); the imago is recorded as Unknown in the original, so no "Alate" section is set. The genus-level description is based mainly on the worker body wall and digestive tract. The page numbers of the Acta Amazonica article are taken from the SciELO page 53(3); the genus-level treatment lies around pages 202–204 (not checked page by page).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The primary generic character is worker dimorphism (major worker and minor worker); the junction between the midgut and the first proctodeal segment (P1) is straight, without a mixed segment; the molar plate and molar prominence region bear hairs and scale-like sculpturing; the gizzard is not developed; the inner wall of P1 is densely covered with short, stout spines directed towards the enteric valve; P3 forms an S-shaped projection before joining P2. All Neotropical Apicotermitinae lack soldiers.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic, the ratio of major to minor about 1:2, both forms common. Both forms have a visible fontanelle, the postclypeus slightly inflated, the head covered with fine short setae; the mandibles bear hairs and scale-like sculpturing in the molar plate and molar prominence region, with a shallow concavity on the anterior side of the mandibles; the apical tooth of the left mandible is as large as the first and second marginal teeth together, the apical tooth of the right mandible larger than the first and second marginal teeth together. The major worker has a square head capsule with about 34 setae, distributed mainly on the anterior sides and the posterior region, the head with lateral nodes; the minor worker has a rounded head capsule with about 14 setae, evenly distributed on the sides of the head. The digestive tract of both worker forms is spherical, the structures similar in size and position. The gizzard has no cuticular armature, with 6 primary pulvilli, the surface of the pulvilli scale-like, with minute spines posteriorly; the muscular layer of the enteric valve is thin, with 6 symmetrical cushions; the Malpighian tubules have 4 separate insertion points, without a nodule; the short stout spines of the inner wall of P1 are densest near the midgut and near P2, their tips directed towards the enteric valve; P3 forms an S-shaped projection before joining P2. Measurements: species-level (LH, WH, LT, WP, see the species-level description).

/genus/cephalotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 84–85). Only one species was known, Cephalotermes rectangularis (Sjöst.) (Cameroon, Congo); the alate section is explicitly marked 'Imago (Königin)', i.e. described from the queen; the note on the Malpighian tubules and hindgut glandular plates in the worker section concerns internal anatomy and has been retained faithfully at the end of the worker section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A monotypic genus, with only Cephalotermes rectangularis (Sjöst.), from Cameroon and the Congo. The soldier head is rectangular and flattened-cylindrical, eyeless, with antennae of 12 segments; the worker mandibles are of the modified Termes type (Hamitermes type), with antennae of 13 segments; the alate has antennae of 14 segments, segment 1 very large and segment 3 small, wings with spines, and the female without exudate hairs. Holmgren's original description is based on the queen (a dealate individual) and points out that, judging from the size of its head and thorax, the alate itself should be fairly small.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Described from the queen (Königin) in the original. Head oval, slightly narrowed anteriorly. Frons flatly convex, slightly depressed in front of the frontal gland opening. Compound eyes medium-sized, fairly flat; ocelli medium-sized, slightly lateral, separated from the compound eyes by hardly more than their larger diameter. Frontal gland opening small and distinct, on the middle of the head. Clypeal base moderately convex, almost as long as half its width, posterior margin fairly strongly convex and anterior margin straight and sharply delimited, brighter than the frons. Labrum wider than long. Mandibular basal segments small; mandibles of the Termes type, the basal tooth of the left mandible weakly developed. Antennae of 14 segments, segment 1 very large, segment 3 small. Pronotum only slightly narrower than the head, head width 0.79 mm, pronotum width 0.7 mm. Posterior margins of the meso- and metanotum with an emargination, the posterior projections blunt and rounded. Forewing scale distinctly longer than the hindwing scale, the wing surface with small spines. Female without exudate hairs; the sides of the queen's abdomen verrucose, seemingly wrinkled, weakly pigmented. Because the abdomen is extremely developed, the queen examined is unusually large.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular, flattened-cylindrical. Frons slightly inclined. Eyeless, cranial suture invisible. Frontal gland opening barely discernible, frontal gland very indistinct and small. Clypeus lens-shaped; labrum quadrangular with rounded anterior corners. Mandibles short and robust, the base large; 2 small teeth on each side in the middle; the left mandible with a small tooth at the base, the base of the right mandible mainly rounded. Antennae slender, of 12 segments, segment 3 shorter and narrower than segment 2 and slightly shorter than segment 4. Pronotum rather small, saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe rather short. Cerci small, without styli. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with 2 each.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Small in size. Head oval, fairly thick, flatly convex; frontal gland opening fairly far back. The length of the clypeal base greater than half its width, convex, the posterior margin very strongly arched and sharply delimited, the anterior margin straight. Labrum small, strongly inclined, wider in the middle than at the base. Mandibles of the modified Termes type (Hamitermes type). Antennae of 13 segments, segment 3 far shorter and narrower than segment 2 and distinctly shorter than segment 4. Pronotum short, far narrower than the head, saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe almost as long as the posterior part. Cerci short, without styli. Note in the original: Malpighian tubules without a collecting vesicle, hindgut segments I–II without glandular plates.

/genus/constrictotermes/.note: A subgenus established by Holmgren 1912 under Eutermes and listed as the 14th subgenus in the catalogue, containing cavifrons Holmgren (Suriname), cyphergaster Silvestri and latinotus Holmgren (Ecuador). The 1912 original gives only key entries and the subgeneric catalogue, with no worker characters, so no Worker section is given. The “position in the key” in the Alate section refers to the key branch and is not a complete description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier head capsule is markedly dumbbell-shaped, constricted behind the antennal fossae, the dorsal cephalic outline in front of the depression being only slightly longer than behind it, the nasus relatively short and conical, antennae 14–15-segmented. This combination suffices to separate it from Coarctotermes (nasus long and thick, conical, antennae 12–13(–14)-segmented, the anterior part of the head much longer than the posterior), Tenuirostritermes (nasus slender, cylindrical, antennae 11–13-segmented) and Grallatotermes (nasus short and very broadly conical, the head not dumbbell-shaped constricted behind the antennae). Alates are distinguished by the broadly oval head, markedly narrowing anteriorly, with a flattened and rounded occiput, together with rather small and strongly protruding compound eyes and a clypeus concolorous with the frons or only slightly paler, from Velocitermes and Tenuirostritermes (head oval, occiput well developed).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, markedly narrowed anteriorly, the occiput flattened and rounded and gently sloping; compound eyes situated on the sides of the head, relatively small and strongly protruding; clypeus shorter than or about equal to half its width, concolorous with the frons or only slightly paler; antennal segments slightly elongate; pronotum relatively large. In the original key, this genus is placed together with Rotunditermes (eyes very large) and Diversitermes (eyes medium-sized) in a branch characterised by “the 1st marginal tooth of the mandible about as long as the 2nd, and the clypeus equal to or slightly shorter than half its width”.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Of the Constrictus group, with a single soldier type. Head capsule dumbbell-shaped, constricted behind the antennal fossae; the dorsal cephalic outline in front of the depression only slightly longer than behind it, the depression itself strong and distinct; nasus relatively short, conical; antennae 14–15-segmented.

/genus/convexitermes/.note: A subgenus established by Holmgren 1912 and listed as the 7th subgenus in the catalogue, containing convexifrons Holmgren (Peru) and nigricornis Holmgren (Peru). The original has no worker characters; the worker clypeal character mentioned in the last sentence of the Soldier section is only a key aid and does not suffice for a Worker section. The Alate and Soldier sections lie in different main key branches and only together form the diagnostic combination of the genus; they must not be taken as a complete description of a single caste.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the key, the alates and soldiers of this genus run in different main branches. In the alate, the 1st marginal tooth of the mandible is distinctly larger than the 2nd, the head is broadly oval and usually narrows anteriorly, and the fontanelle lies far back on the head; the soldiers are small species with no apical part on the mandibles, a short, thick, conical nasus, 11-segmented antennae and a convex frontal profile. On this basis the soldier is distinguished from Occasitermes (nasus long and thick, conical, antennae 13-segmented, frontal profile straight) and Eutermellus (head slightly constricted behind the antennae).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The 1st marginal tooth of the mandible distinctly larger than the 2nd; head broadly oval, usually narrowing anteriorly; fontanelle far back on the head; brain well developed within the head (given as Gehirn stark entwickelt in the original); clypeus about as long as half its width, or shorter but strongly convex, transversely oval and pale yellow.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Small species. Mandibles without an apical part (Spitzenteil); nasus short, thick, conical; antennae 11-segmented; frontal profile (Stirnprofil) convex. The key additionally uses the worker clypeus, whose base is about as long as half its width, as an auxiliary character of the branch containing this genus.

/genus/cornitermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 49–50). Cornitermes in the original includes the two subgenera Labiotermes and Cornitermes s. str., the generic characters being common to both; the key to species and subgenera is not included in the description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate relatively large, wings hyaline; antennae 15–17 segments; base of clypeus strongly arched, as long as half its width; mandibular first tooth sometimes larger than the second, third tooth of the left mandible stepped. Soldier head more or less rectangular, frontal gland opening large, at the apex of a long or short frontal tube, antennae 13–15 segments, third segment usually shorter than the second; all tibiae with only 2 apical spurs, styli absent. Holmgren 1912 divided the genus into two subgenera, Labiotermes and Cornitermes s. str.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Relatively large, wings hyaline. Head broadly oval, narrowing anteriorly; compound eyes projecting; ocelli lateral, medium-sized to very large, close to the compound eyes or fairly far from them. Frontal gland opening large and distinct. Base of clypeus as long as half its width, strongly arched, posterior margin strongly convex, anterior margin mostly straight, labrum broader than long. Mandibular first tooth sometimes larger than the second, third tooth of the left mandible stepped, molar region rather well developed. Antennae 15–17 segments, third segment shorter to longer than the second. Pronotum narrower than the head, flat, anterior corners only slightly deflexed; posterior margins of meso- and metanotum broad, more or less broadly rounded. Wings hyaline, only the costa and the radial sector dark and distinct, the remaining veins hyaline and weak; wing membrane rather densely covered with fine hairs; radius reduced, hardly extending beyond the wing scale; radial sector somewhat distant from the anterior margin; media of forewing arising beyond the wing scale, media of hindwing arising at the base of the radial sector, sometimes branching at or before the middle of the wing; cubitus without a thickened basal vein, or only very weakly so. All tibiae with only 2 apical spurs. Cerci short, styli absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head more or less rectangular, rather thick. Frontal gland opening large, at the apex of a long or short frontal tube; the frons in front of the tube slopes gradually towards the mouthparts. Clypeus almost indistinguishable from the transverse band, apex often corneous, always supported by two anteriorly diverging chitinous bands. Labrum either elongate and narrowing anteriorly, or shorter, widest at the middle, apex hyaline. Mandibles stout, sickle-shaped: left mandible with 2 to several incisor teeth, sometimes with a large base; right mandible often with its middle and base fused into a large masticatory part. Antennae 13–15 segments, third segment usually shorter than the second, sometimes equal or longer. Pronotum narrower than the head, weakly saddle-shaped, anterior lobe very large, reaching the neck. Tibiae with 2 apical spurs; cerci short; styli absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head pale yellow to white, subcircular to pentagonal and rounded, widest at the level of the antennae, flattened and arched. Clypeus large and arched. Mandibular first tooth either not larger than the second or distinctly larger. Antennae 14–16 segments, mostly 15. Pronotum as in the soldier; meso- and metanotum strongly compressed by the strongly arched abdomen.

/genus/crenetermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 101–102). The Chinese generic name is not yet fixed, so zh_name provisionally uses the Latin name in the form of a Chinese common name, pending confirmation at a higher level. Only one species, Crenetermes albotarsalis (Sjöst.), is known, from Cameroon and the Congo; p. 102 is entirely a discussion of systematic relationships with the Mirotermes series and contains no morphological description, so it was not used.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus, with only Crenetermes albotarsalis (Sjöst.), from Cameroon and the Congo; synonyms include Eutermes albotarsalis Sjöst. and Suleitermes Wasm. (an unpublished name) in the literature. Alate head subquadrate, antennae 16 segments with the third short; soldier head rectangular, longer than broad, labrum subquadrate and strongly grooved, mandibles of the same type as Thoracotermes, antennae 15 segments; worker entirely white, head longer than broad, mandibles with a large apical tooth. Holmgren placed the genus in the Mirotermes series, but the soldier mandibles have Termes-type teeth and the frontal gland opening is exposed and not situated beneath a frontal protuberance, differing from all the Mirotermes subgenera and from Thoracotermes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head width about equal to the length. Compound eyes small, projecting. Ocelli about their own diameter from the compound eyes. Base of clypeus brighter than the frons, very large, slightly longer than half its width (9:8.5), very strongly arched; because the base of the clypeus is expanded, the malar part of the head appears short. Mandibular first tooth large. Antennae 16 segments, third short. The incision of the posterior margin of the mesonotum is broader than that of the metanotum. Wings dark, the membrane with fine dense small spine-like points (»punktiert« in the original). Media of forewing arising independently behind the wing scale. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with 2 each. Cerci short. Styli absent. The original adds: a reduced stylus was once observed in a male nymph.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head longer than broad, quadrangular, narrowing slightly anteriorly, rather arched, anterior margin obliquely truncate. Frontal gland opening on the margin of the sloping frons, rather small but densely surrounded by hairs. Base of clypeus completely flat, slightly shorter than half its width. Labrum subquadrate, widening slightly outwards, strongly grooved; anterior margin slightly incised in the middle, the lateral angles only indistinctly acute, directed anteriorly. Mandibles as in Thoracotermes. Antennae 15 segments, third short. Pronotum deeply saddle-shaped, small. Tibial spur formula as in the alate. Styli absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Entirely white. Head longer than broad. Base of clypeus about as long as half its width, strongly arched. Mandibles with a large apical tooth. Antennae 15 segments, third short. Pronotum deeply saddle-shaped. Tibial spur formula and condition of the styli as above (styli absent).

/genus/cyranotermes/.note: Rocha, Carrijo & Cancello 2012 (Zootaxa 3196: 50–57) is the most recent revision of the genus and first described the alate, but only page 1 of its PDF (abstract and introduction) could be obtained through the text proxy and the body of the generic diagnosis was not read, so this entry gives soldier characters only, based on the soldier key of Constantino 1999, and does not supply Alate or Worker sections.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head capsule narrow, oval, the frontal tube conical and thick at the base; in contrast, Anhangatermes has a very broad, round head capsule and a nearly cylindrical frontal tube that is narrow at the base. This contrast is exactly the position of the genus in the Neotropical soldier key.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule narrow and oval in dorsal view; frontal tube conical, thick at the base. In the key the genus is the counterpart entry to Anhangatermes, which has a very broad, round head capsule and a nearly cylindrical frontal tube narrow at the base.

/genus/disjunctitermes/.note: The imago is recorded as Unknown in the original, so no "Alate" section is set; there is no soldier section (soldierless). The genus-level Diagnosis deals mainly with the enteric valve and the tibia, and the genus-level Worker section gives the body wall and digestive tract.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among Neotropical apicotermitines, like Anoplotermes banksi, A. pacificus and Hydrecotermes spp., it has a strongly inflated fore tibia, and an enteric valve without spines and without sclerotisation. It is closest to A. banksi but can be distinguished from it by the accessory (fourth) marginal tooth of the left mandible, the larger enteric valve seating and the more truncate end of P2; Hydrecotermes lacks a spherical mesenteric tongue.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic, small. Head capsule pale yellow, covered with about 100 setae of varying length; postclypeus moderately inflated; fontanelle almost indiscernible; antennae 14-segmented. The apical tooth and the first marginal tooth of the left mandible are widely separated and both long, clearly projecting beyond the line formed by the third marginal tooth and the molar prominence; above the molar prominence there is another accessory (fourth) marginal tooth, visible in both dorsal and ventral view. The apical tooth of the right mandible is far longer than the first marginal tooth, the third marginal tooth nearly symmetrical. The fore tibia is strongly inflated, about 3 times as long as its greatest width (at the middle). The mesenteric tongue is spherical. P2 enters through a large, stout, trilobed enteric valve seating, two lobes of which are visible through the body wall; the enteric valve consists of 6 slender, inflated pads facing the valve lumen; the posterior end of P2 (including the enteric valve) is truncate and extends about halfway into the seating. Measurements: species-level (Table 2, 12 workers from each of 11 colonies; holotype head width 0.64 mm).

/genus/diversitermes/.note: Established by Holmgren 1912 and listed as the 9th subgenus in the catalogue, containing diversimilis Silvestri (Paraguay, Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia) and castaniceps Holmgren (Brazil). The original contains only key entries and gives no measurements for the three soldier types, so only the number of types and qualitative characters are given above; the original also has no worker characters.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The most conspicuous feature is the trimorphism of the soldier: in the major soldier the nasus is narrow and slender with a weak basal depression; in the medium and minor soldiers the head capsule is more or less dumbbell-shaped constricted; antennae 13-segmented; the legs of the two small soldier types are rather long. In the same group Velocitermes is dimorphic (corresponding to the medium and minor types of this genus) and Trinervitermes is dimorphic or rarely trimorphic but has no apical part on the mandibles; the three fixed soldier types remain the most conspicuous mark of this genus. The alate is distinguished from Rotunditermes (eyes very large) by the medium-sized eyes, the 1st marginal tooth of the mandible about as long as the 2nd, and the clypeus about as long as half its width.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes medium-sized (the original key contrasts them with the very large eyes of Rotunditermes, and that branch additionally records the compound eyes as bulging dorsolaterally on the head and the pronotum as relatively large); the 1st marginal tooth of the mandible about as long as the 2nd; clypeus about as long as half its width, or slightly shorter and strongly convex, transversely oval, pale yellow and sometimes dark; antennal segments with average elongation.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier trimorphic. Major soldier: nasus narrow, basal depression weak. Medium and minor soldiers: head capsule more or less markedly dumbbell-shaped constricted; antennae 13-segmented. The legs of the two small soldier types are rather long.

/genus/diwaitermes/.note: The generic characters are given in three sections, Imago / Soldier / Worker, as in the original; only the type species of the alate is known and it has no morphological description, so that section records only what the original says about this caste and contains no measurements. The original notes that N. orientis is almost certainly a junior synonym of Eutermes kanehirae Oshima, 1914, and the generic characters follow N. orientis; the genus contains three species, D. kanehirae, D. foi and D. castanopsis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Roisin & Pasteels established the genus with Nasutitermes (Subulitermes) orientis from New Guinea as type species, the generic name being taken from the New Melanesian word diwai (wood). The soldier is fully nasute and closely related to Nasutitermes, but the head capsule is not constricted behind the antennal fossae, the soldier is monomorphic, small to medium in size, and the antennae are 11- or 12-segmented. What really separates it from Nasutitermes and Niuginitermes is the worker gut: the mesenteric part of the mixed segment is attached by a broad stalk dorsally and slightly mesally on the midgut, the 4 Malpighian tubules converge where they attach at the midgut–hindgut junction, and the two rings of spines on the enteric valve are asymmetric, with the lower ring of spines projecting into the stomach lumen; the worker is dimorphic. Eleanoritermes from Borneo resembles the genus, but its worker mandibles have a more concave molar region, its enteric valve is placed further forward, only three swellings bear a few small spines, and the colon is longer.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Only the type species is known. The original lists no genus-level morphological characters and only notes that the number of antennal segments may later serve to distinguish the genus from Nasutitermes and Niuginitermes. The original also compares the closely related Nasutitermes liklik: it differs from D. kanehirae in having one more antennal segment in every caste (14 versus 13 in the alate).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Fully nasute, closely related to Nasutitermes. Head capsule not constricted behind the antennal fossae; soldier monomorphic, small to medium in size; antennae 11- or 12-segmented, and when 12-segmented segment 3 is extremely short and incompletely separated from segment 4; head capsule hairy, with many setae of varying length; the points on the mandibles are small and sometimes absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae 12- or 13-segmented, and when 13-segmented segment 3 is extremely short and incompletely separated from segment 4. Mandibles very similar to those of Nasutitermes, left mandible index 0.45–0.55. Gut: the mesenteric part of the mixed segment is attached by a broad stalk dorsally and slightly mesally on the rest of the midgut; the 4 Malpighian tubules converge where they attach at the midgut–hindgut junction; the upper ring of spines on the enteric valve is slightly asymmetric, and the lower ring of spines projects into the stomach lumen. Worker dimorphic; the body length distribution of the major worker is unimodal, with no growth and a slight darkening of pigmentation within the same instar.

/genus/dolichorhinotermes/.note: The alate section rests only on the diagnostic statement at generic level (the 3rd flagellar segment shorter than the 1st) and on the account of the fossil species D. apopnus; the original states explicitly that the alate of the extant species is unknown. Page 2 is in two columns and the text layer was reflowed after column-wise cropping; hyphens broken across lines in the quotation (subquad-rate) have been rejoined, with no change to the wording.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the alate the 3rd flagellar segment is shorter than the 1st flagellar segment; in the major soldier the labrum is distinctly elongate, its apex often reaching the ends of the mandibles, whereas the labrum of Rhinotermes is almost square and much shorter; in the minor soldier the opening of the frontal gland lies on the anterior part of the head but is not borne on a distinct frontal projection, the mandibles are reduced with rounded margins, and in dorsal view the sides of the head are straight or convex.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The 3rd flagellar segment is shorter than the 1st flagellar segment. For the extant species D. lanciarius the original records the alate as 'Imago. Unknown.'; the alate of the fossil species D. apopnus: head large, broad and rounded, the anteclypeus projecting forwards as a broad beak-like process, the frontal gland small and situated at the base of the beak, the compound eyes large and protruding, the ocelli large and elongate and not touching the compound eyes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: posterior part of the head broader, the sides gently rounded and narrowing forwards; left mandible with two coarse teeth, the first just before mid-length and the second slightly behind it, the first distinctly longer than the second; right mandible with two teeth near mid-length, the first shorter than the second; labrum elongate with a rounded apex, without an incision, and with a shallow longitudinal groove dorsally; antennae with at least 14 segments, the 3rd flagellar segment distinctly shorter than the 1st; pronotum saddle-shaped. Minor soldier: sides of the head weakly convex and narrowing forwards, the posterior margin rounded; antennae 16 segments, the 3rd flagellar segment distinctly shorter than the 1st; mandibles reduced to broad fleshy lobes bearing only minute sclerotised points; labrum narrow and long, forked at the apex, the two prongs widely separated.

/genus/drepanotermes/.note: Proposed in the original as a subgenus of HAMITERMES (Untergattung Drepanotermes); the genus diagnosis is given for the soldier and worker, the alate is unknown. The German genus diagnosis is rewritten from OCR text, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Relatively large in size; alate unknown. Soldier: head rectangular, flatly convex; postclypeus bilobed; labrum oval and slightly pointed; mandibles very long, strongly sickle-curved and slender, with 1 long, obliquely truncate tooth almost at the middle, perpendicular to the inner margin; antennae 17-segmented; fore tibia with 3 apical spurs. Worker: head large, broadly oval; fontanelle and sagittal suture very conspicuous; postclypeus very large and arched; antennae 18-segmented.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Relatively large in size; colour more or less dark. Head rectangular, flatly convex; fontanelle indistinct; pale ocular spots behind the eyes. Postclypeus bilobed. Labrum oval, slightly pointed. Mandibles very long, strongly sickle-curved, slender, with 1 long, obliquely truncate tooth almost at the middle, perpendicular to the inner margin. Antennae 17-segmented, segments elongate; segment 2 as long as segments 3 and 4 together. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head, concolorous; remaining tergites slightly paler. Legs long; fore tibia with 3 apical spurs.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: As large as or slightly larger than the soldier, same colour, legs long. Head large, broadly oval; fontanelle very distinct; sagittal suture very distinct, transverse suture indistinct; ocelli vestigial. Pale ocular spots behind the antennae. Postclypeus very large, arched, margins pale; labrum wider than long, pale. Antennae 18-segmented, segment 2 as long as segments 3 and 4 together, segment 3 distinctly longer than segment 4, segment 5 slightly longer than segment 3. Pronotum much narrower than the head. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs.

/genus/duplidentitermes/.note: The original gives the genus diagnosis by comparison with Hoplognathotermes and Allognathotermes. Rewritten from the English genus diagnosis, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to Hoplognathotermes and Allognathotermes; the soldier differs most conspicuously from the closely related genera in having 1 large bicuspid tooth on each mandible; antennae 13–14-segmented; fore femur short and stout, equally thick at the middle; sharp ridge of the fore coxa with 9–11 conspicuous setae in a row. The alate and the worker mandibles show corresponding features.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Fore coxa with several short hairs and long and short setae on its outline; middle tibia without contrasting outer spines. Fontanelle white, triangular, only slightly smaller than the ocellus. Mandibles broadly similar to those of the worker: apical tooth proportionally larger than in Hoplognathotermes; in the left mandible the distance from the apical point to the first marginal tooth point is greater than that from the first to the third marginal tooth point; cutting edges of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible undulating; second marginal tooth of the right mandible reduced to a small mound (as in Allognathotermes). Posterior margins of meso- and metanotum deeply concave, the notch angle sharper than a right angle. Fore coxa with a sharp longitudinal ridge, flatly convex in section, the crest of the ridge nearer the base than the middle of the ridge. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2, outer spur of the fore tibia short and distinctly reduced. Sc short in both fore- and hindwing, merging with the anterior margin immediately after the basal suture.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head very large, anterior face rather flat; no tuft of hairs near the frontal gland opening; setae at the front end of the large labrum scattered, not in tufts as in Apicotermes; sharp ridge of the fore coxa with 9–11 conspicuous setae in 1 row, curved towards the inner margin and back towards the apex, enclosing a nearly oval flat area in the apical half of the coxa. Inner side of the fore tibia with several weakly specialised spines; middle tibia without contrasting outer spines. Anterior part of the postmentum proportionally larger than in the closely related genera, the narrowest point about 5/6–6/7 of its length from the anterior margin, lateral sutures visible over their whole length. Antennae 13–14-segmented, similar to Allognathotermes (Firmitermes 14-segmented, Hoplognathotermes and Acutidentitermes 15-segmented). Suture between postclypeus and frons visible, but less distinct than in Firmitermes and Hoplognathotermes. Labrum widest at the distinct lateral angles (in Firmitermes the labral lateral margins are convex, in Hoplognathotermes the sides are parallel with obtuse lateral angles, in Acutidentitermes the sides are parallel and slightly concave with a sharper apex, in Allognathotermes the widest point is rounder). Each mandible with 1 large bicuspid tooth, by which it differs conspicuously from all closely related genera. Longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa conspicuous and sharp, gently and evenly convex in section, extending about half the coxa from the apex, more arched and more distinct than in Hoplognathotermes, and very similar to Allognathotermes, only slightly more evident because it extends with a slight inward curve. Fore femur short and stout, sides parallel, equally thick at the middle; fore tibia slightly swollen. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2, outer spur of the fore tibia proportionally short (as in Hoplognathotermes).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibular features similar to those of the alate; ridge of the fore coxa more arched and more projecting than in the Hoplognathotermes worker.

/genus/ekueitermes/.note: The imago is recorded as Unknown in the original, so no "Alate" section is set; there is no soldier section (soldierless). The original also has a Comparison and remarks section, pointing out that the digestive tract is similar to that of Patawatermes and Hirsutitermes, but that the EVS is shorter.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The mesenteric tongue of the mixed segment is short and not inflated; P1 is very short; the enteric valve armature (EVA) consists of 6 conical cushions, each covered with 18–25 polygonal scales with fringed margins (4–15 per cushion), the distal end of each cushion with 7–17 sclerotised spines arranged in palmate fashion; the enteric valve seating (EVS) is distinctly differentiated and tubular.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic, medium-sized (head length and head width from medium to large). Head capsule pale white to pale yellow, densely covered with evenly spaced long, fine, pale, erect setae interspersed with short hairs; in lateral view the dorsum slightly concave, the antennal segments translucent. Antennae 14-segmented, segment formula 2>3<4<5. Fontanelle distinct, oval, situated behind the brain (visible in preserved specimens); postclypeus strongly inflated. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior and posterior margins with rows of long fine erect setae, the lateral margins with several long setae; the anterior lobe margins of the mesonotum and metanotum also with rows of setae. Abdomen transparent, the tergites and sternites densely covered with setae of varying length. Fore coxa and fore femur with numerous pale fine setae; fore tibia strongly inflated, interspersed with a few long setae and numerous minute dense setae; the tibial spines of all legs weak, indistinct except apically; apical spur formula 2:2:2. The apical tooth of the left mandible is more projecting than M1+2, forming an acute angle with it, the posterior margin of M1+2 slightly concave; M3 less projecting than M1+2, its margin forming an acute angle; molar prominence well developed, not concealing the molar process in dorsal view. The apical tooth of the right mandible is more projecting than M1, M1 small and slightly exceeding M2, a right angle between M1 and M2, the posterior margin of M2 concave, without a ridge. Digestive tract: crop large; mixed segment short and not inflated; midgut short and narrow, gradually widening into a very short, tubular P1 that does not form a ventral loop; EVS well differentiated, tubular; P3 large and inflated, P4 very long and narrow, P5 saccular. Measurements: species-level (Table 1, 17 workers from 3 colonies).

/genus/eremotermes/.note: The original records the alate as unknown and gives only the nymph (antennae 14-segmented, head oval, fontanelle very far back, postclypeal basis about half as long as wide, first tooth of the left mandible slightly larger than the second). The German genus diagnosis is rewritten from OCR text, with technical terms rendered according to standard insect morphology usage.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate unknown (only the nymph known). Soldier: head shaped as in Mirotermes, short-cylindrical, with a distinct, rounded frontal projection, beneath which lies a rather large fontanelle opening; labrum triangular rather than bilobed; mandibles long and rod-like, symmetrical, with 1 sharp tooth at the middle directed inwards and slightly backwards; antennae 14-segmented; pronotum saddle-shaped, abdomen very thick, nearly spherical, legs short, tibiae with 2 apical spurs.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head as in Mirotermes, short-cylindrical, with a distinct, rounded-obtuse frontal projection, beneath which lies a rather large fontanelle opening; head hairy, the hairs denser around the fontanelle; frons descending gently forwards beneath the frontal projection. Fontanelle gland very large, extending posteriorly to the back of the neck. Labrum triangular (not bilobed as in Mirotermes). Mandibles long and rod-like, apex only slightly incurved, symmetrical; with 1 sharp tooth at the middle directed inwards and slightly backwards; mandibular base very long, as long as the rest; the boundary between base and the main body of the mandible marked by a small bend in the outer margin; molar region step-like, quadrangular. Antennae 14-segmented. Pronotum saddle-shaped. Abdomen very thick, almost spherical, its sides bulging out like inflated sacs; legs short; tibiae with 2 apical spurs; cerci short, without styli.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head thick, broadly oval; fontanelle very far back; postclypeal basis with length equal to half its width, rather strongly arched; first mandibular tooth slightly larger than the second; antennae relatively short, with crowded segments, 14-segmented; pronotum saddle-shaped, abdomen rather thick.

/genus/eurytermes/.note: In the OCR the later part of the soldier section and the worker section are affected by two-column misalignment; only sentences that can be read continuously have been taken, and gaps are not filled in. The German genus diagnosis is rewritten, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate: head nearly circular, narrowing in a straight line anteriorly, frons rather strongly arched, compound eyes small and strongly projecting, fontanelle distinct and far back (hence the median transverse band rather long); antennae 15-segmented (or 14), segment 3 distinctly shorter than segment 2. Soldier: head thick, rectangular, eyeless, cranial sutures invisible, fontanelle almost indistinct; labrum triangular, mandibles rather short and stout, left mandible with 1 large, strong, anteriorly directed tooth before the midpoint; antennae very fine, 14-segmented. Worker: head oval, length barely exceeding width.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head nearly circular, narrowing in a straight line anteriorly; frons rather strongly arched; compound eyes small, strongly projecting; ocelli small, about their own diameter from the compound eye, inner margin slightly raised. Fontanelle distinct, far back, hence the median transverse band rather long. Postclypeal basis rather arched, length equal to half its width or slightly less, posterior margin rather strongly arcuate. Labrum at the middle barely wider than at the base, without a chitinous transverse band. Mandibles with the Termes-type armature, base not very developed. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 much shorter than segment 2 and slightly shorter than segment 4 (or 14-segmented, in which case segment 3 as long as segment 2). Pronotum narrower and smaller than the head, anterior margin straight, only slightly upfolded; meso- and metanotum with only a very narrow triangular emargination; posterior angles pointed, not rounded. Forewing scale only slightly longer than the hindwing scale; wings covered with fine hairs; in the forewing the media arises directly from the wing scale (exceptionally from the radial sector), in the hindwing the media arises from the radial sector; media closer to the radial sector than to the cubitus. Cerci short, without styli. Female densely covered with glandular setae, male also but more sparsely. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs. Body rather slender.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head thick, rectangular; eyeless; cranial sutures invisible; fontanelle almost indistinct; postclypeus short. Labrum triangular, rather short, without a hyaline apical point. Mandibles rather short and stout; left mandible with 1 large, strong, anteriorly directed tooth before the midpoint, with a trace of a tooth on its basal side; right mandible with 1 slightly obtuse tooth. Antennae very fine, 14-segmented, segment 2 only slightly longer than segment 5. Pronotum barely reaching half the head width, with a large anterior lobe. Cerci short, without styli.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head oval, length barely exceeding width, convex; frons concave above it.

/genus/eutermellus/.note: Sands 1965 provides three sections, Imago, Soldier and Worker, all entered as in the original. The left mandible index of the alate is given in the original as 96–98 (percentage scale) and that of the worker as 1.24–1.62 (ratio scale); the two differ in dimension and have been recorded as they stand without conversion.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands regarded the genus as the least specialised member of the African Paracornitermes group: the mandibles of the alate and worker, the Y-shaped fontanelle typical of some species, the trilobed anterior margin of the soldier labrum and the generally more numerous setae all point to this. It differs from Vernicositermes and Afrosubulitermes in the denser pilosity (and in size). The soldier is monomorphic, with a conical to cylindrical nasus tapering to a fine, distinctly wrinkled point, a trilobed anterior margin of the labrum, 13-segmented antennae, and a head very weakly to moderately constricted behind the antennae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The apical tooth of the left mandible is distinctly longer than the 1st marginal tooth, but the distance between them is slightly shorter than that between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth (left mandible index 96–98); the cutting edge between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth is wavy and concave in front of the 3rd marginal tooth, which is nearly equilateral, and a very small subsidiary tooth is visible in the gap between it and the molar prominence. The right mandible has the apical tooth and 1st marginal tooth as in the left, the 2nd marginal tooth small but distinct with a concave posterior edge; the surface of the molar plate has no basal concavity and is asymmetric, its posterior edge forming a large rounded wing and its anterior wing smaller, the ridges weak. Postclypeus convex, 1.8–2.5 times as wide as long. Fontanelle variable in shape: Y-shaped, triangular, dumbbell-shaped or nearly absent. The degree to which the compound eyes protrude from the sides of the head ranges from almost none to distinct. The cephalic pilosity is irregular in length, the conspicuous long setae often arranged in symmetrical pairs. The sides of the pronotum converge weakly towards the rounded posterior margin, the pronotum being about two-thirds as long as wide.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic. Nasus conical to cylindrical, tapering to a fine point and distinctly wrinkled. Vestigial mandibles with a minute point or with no point at all; anterior margin of the labrum trilobed. Head capsule very weakly to moderately constricted behind the antennae. Antennae 13-segmented. Head and nasus covered with sparse, extremely short fine hairs, longer at the tip of the nasus; in addition, conspicuous longer setae are arranged roughly in two rows, one in front of the constriction (4–10) and one behind it (2–10).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibles as in the alate, but with a proportionally longer apical tooth (left mandible index 1.24–1.62) and a more developed molar region.

/genus/firmitermes/.note: The original gives the provisional assignment '?Firmitermes', and the generic characters of the alate are accordingly conditional; that premise is retained in the rewriting. The original has no genus-level worker description. Rewritten from the English generic characters, not a literal translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is closely allied to Hoplognathotermes and shows no genus-level difference in head shape, but the pilosity of the face of the head, the postmentum and the fore coxae is far richer, the postmentum bears transverse wrinkles over its whole length, the labrum is broad and rounded, without lateral angles or apical projections, and the base of the mandibles is short and thick; the alate is described only on the basis of the provisionally assigned 'Eutermes' tripolitanus, whose left mandible has a third marginal tooth proportionally far larger than in any known genus of the Amitermitinae or the Termitinae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The following generic characters presuppose the provisional assignment of 'Eutermes' tripolitanus to this genus. The apical teeth of both mandibles are smaller and finer than in the workers of Hoplognathotermes and Acutidentitermes and lie closer to the first marginal tooth; the angle between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth of the left mandible is more acute; the actual lengths of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible are similar to those of Acutidentitermes, but the notch before the third marginal tooth is less sharp and the apical margin of the third marginal tooth is longer (that of Acutidentitermes being distinctly convex and short); the third marginal tooth is proportionally far larger than in any known genus of the Amitermitinae or the Termitinae; beneath the concave ridge between the third marginal tooth and the molar plate of the left mandible there are 2 small projections, with a concave margin between them (Acutidentitermes has only 1 projection beneath the basal molar plate); the first marginal tooth of the right mandible shows traces of a reduced accessory tooth near the angle where it meets the apical tooth; the second marginal tooth is concave on both its anterior and posterior margins, whereas that of Acutidentitermes is convex and blunt with nearly straight margins; the concavity of the upper margin of the basal plate of the right mandible is weaker than in Acutidentitermes. The fore tibiae each bear 3 spurs, the mid and hind tibiae 2 each.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The face, vertex, sides of the head and postmentum bear numerous scattered short hairs and setae, whereas in Hoplognathotermes subterraneus and Acutidentitermes osborni the face bears very few setae and the postmentum is almost hairless. On the fore coxa, the section of the flat-convex apical part shows 3–4 setae, the section of the sharply convex basal part bears a few setae and short hairs, the longitudinal ridge is rounded and blunt, and a few very short hairs are visible when the coxa is rotated. The head shape shows no genus-level difference from Hoplognathotermes, the anterior part being flatter, without marked ridges or tubercles; the fontanelle is small and indistinct. The postmentum is constricted in the middle, its sides fairly concave (slightly deeper than in Hoplognathotermes), and bears a series of indistinct transverse wrinkles over its whole length, whereas H. subterraneus has transverse wrinkles only posteriorly and the postmentum of A. osborni is globular and without transverse wrinkles. The labrum is proportionally as broad as in H. subterraneus but its margin is more rounded, without the lateral angles and apical projection of the latter or of A. osborni.
