The postclypeus is distinct and the suture between it and the frons is not lost. The base of the mandibles is proportionally short and thick, the outer margin fairly strongly convex, and the junction between the apical and basal parts lacks the angular notch found in Hoplognathotermes or Acutidentitermes; the apical process is shorter and thicker than in either, its outer margin more curved; the tooth base of the type specimen is broken off, so the tooth form cannot be known, but the small notch between the apical margin and the tooth of the right mandible indicates an angle close to that of H. subterraneus and unlike the more acute angle of A. osborni; the tooth-like projection at the base is indistinct or absent. The pronotum is smaller and narrower than in H. subterraneus, its anterior lobe equally large and the median concavity of its anterior margin equally small and shallow; the angle between the anterior lobe and the posterior part in lateral view is less acute than in H. subterraneus, being nearly flat-concave. The fore coxa has no projection, its longitudinal ridge being fairly rounded and blunt, not as sharp and long as in H. subterraneus; the section of the ridge is flat-convex from the trochanteral region to the middle and turns flat-concave towards the basal outer angle. The fore tibiae bear 3 apical spurs, the outer spur extremely short and visible only on careful manipulation; the mid and hind tibiae bear 2 each.

/genus/fulleritermes/.note: The generic diagnosis of Sands 1965 has only two sections, Imago and Soldier, and no worker is described at genus level, so no Worker section is given. The original lists four species, contractus, coatoni, mallyi and tenebricus, and notes that the genus occupies savanna and drier vegetation zones.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Coaton 1962 separated the genus from Coarctotermes on the incision of the cutting edge of the alate left mandible in front of the 3rd marginal tooth; the same feature occurs in Grallatotermes and Leptomyxotermes, but the compound eyes and ocelli of those two genera are much larger, and Grallatotermes has 13–14 ridges on the right molar plate. The molar plate of this genus has 7–9 ridges and a very weak to very strong concavity on the anterior edge near the base, the 1st molar ridge forming a coarse tooth. The soldier is monomorphic or dimorphic, the nasus cylindrical or conical, the head ranging from almost unconstricted to strongly constricted behind the antennae, the posterior lobe usually more than a quarter wider than the anterior part, antennae 12–13-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The apical tooth of the left mandible is as long as the 1st marginal tooth, and the distance from the apical tooth to the 1st marginal tooth is more than one-third of the distance between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth (left mandible index 36–43); the cutting edge between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth bears an incision that delimits the 3rd marginal tooth. The right mandible has the apical tooth and 1st marginal tooth nearly equal in length, the 1st marginal tooth bearing a small subsidiary tooth at its basal junction near the apical tooth, and the relative lengths of the cutting edges of the 1st and 2nd marginal teeth are variable; the surface of the molar plate has a very weak to very strong concavity on the anterior edge near the base, the posterior edge extending into a rounded wing, the 1st molar ridge forming a coarse tooth, the remaining 7–9 diminishing towards the base. Fontanelle slit-like, distinctly forked anteriorly, usually paler than the head.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic or dimorphic. Nasus cylindrical or conical. Vestigial mandibles with a small to medium-sized point. Head capsule from almost unconstricted to strongly constricted behind the antennae, the posterior lobe usually more than a quarter wider than the anterior part. Antennae 12–13-segmented.

/genus/glossotermes/.note: The original is the original description based on a single holotype soldier and records the alate explicitly as unknown, so no alate or worker sections are given. It was then placed in the Rhinotermitidae and is now assigned to the Serritermitidae; the change of classification does not affect the morphological description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original considers this genus closest to Psammotermes (then placed in the Rhinotermitidae), though the relationship is rather distant; when the genus was established only the soldier was known, the alate being unknown. The soldier is characterised by the combination of a nearly square, slightly flattened head, a distinct eye spot behind each antennal socket, an extremely broad labrum, mandibles only slightly hooked, and a large groove at the base of the left mandible that receives the tooth of the right mandible.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head nearly square and slightly flattened, the sides nearly parallel and slightly convex, reddish brownish yellow; a distinct eye spot behind each antennal socket, smaller than the socket, the ommatidia almost indiscernible; two pale spots above the eye, possibly vestigial ocelli; antennae 13 segments, the terminal segment distinctly narrower than the preceding one, segment 3 about equal to segment 2, segment 4 shorter than segment 3; postclypeus distinct, about 3 times as wide as long; labrum extremely broad, rounded at the sides, with a thin hyaline margin at the apex; mandibles broad at the base, tapering towards the apex and only slightly hooked, with a notch on the outer margin of each at about 2/9 of its length, dividing it into a basal and an apical part; right mandible with a tooth-like process on the inner margin at 1/3 of the length from the base; left mandible finely serrate on the inner margin behind the apex, with a large groove at the base that receives the tooth of the right mandible; pronotum gently arched, distinctly notched at the anterior margin; tibial apical spurs 2:2:2 on all legs. Measurements of the holotype soldier (mm): head length (to the lateral base of the mandibles) 1.56, head height 0.82, head width 1.10, postclypeus length 0.19 and width 0.57, labrum width 0.57, left mandible length 1.09, pronotum width 0.78, hind tibia length 1.09.

/genus/grallatotermes/.note: The generic diagnosis of Sands 1965 contains two sections, Imago and Soldier, and no worker is described at genus level, so no Worker section is given. The original places the genus together with Hospitalitermes in a group with the head capsule constricted behind the antennae, and notes that its alate mandibles are unique among the African species. The key of Holmgren 1912 gives a separate description of the soldier (nasus short and very broadly conical, antennae 13-segmented, head not dumbbell-shaped constricted behind the antennae), which differs in degree from Sands's “nasus thick but only weakly conical, head slightly constricted”; the account above follows the generic diagnosis of Sands.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands regarded its alate mandibles as a unique combination among the African species: the cutting edge of the left mandible has a deep incision between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth, and the right molar plate has 13–14 ridges with no obvious irregularity in surface outline. The incision is shared with Fulleritermes and Leptomyxotermes, but this genus has the most molar ridges (Fulleritermes 7–9, with a concavity on the anterior edge of the molar plate near the base; Leptomyxotermes 6–7, with very large compound eyes and ocelli). The soldier is monomorphic, the nasus thick but only weakly conical, sharply tapering at the tip, the head slightly constricted behind the antennae, and the setae confined to 4 at the tip of the nasus and paired hairs on the postclypeus and vertex.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The apical tooth of the left mandible is slightly shorter than the 1st marginal tooth, the distance between them being about one-quarter of that between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth (left mandible index about 25); the 2nd marginal tooth is delimited by a deep incision in front of the 3rd marginal tooth, and the small subsidiary tooth connecting the 3rd marginal tooth with the molar prominence lies, seen from above, behind the gap between the two. In the right mandible the apical tooth and 1st marginal tooth are nearly equal in length, the posterior cutting edge of the 1st marginal tooth is shorter than that of the 2nd and does not overlap the anterior edge of the 2nd marginal tooth (the surface overlap being buried in a smooth, shining fused surface); the outline of the molar plate in surface view shows no obvious irregularity, with 13–14 ridges diminishing posteriorly. Postclypeus short, slightly convex, about one-third as long as wide. Fontanelle pale, slightly T-shaped. Pronotum with an almost non-convex anterior margin. Cephalic pilosity sparse, fine and uniform, with only a few more conspicuous setae.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic. Nasus thick but only weakly conical, sharply tapering at the tip. Vestigial mandibles with a point. Head capsule slightly constricted behind the antennae; setae only 4 at the tip of the nasus, plus those arranged in pairs on the postclypeus and the two sides of the vertex.

/genus/heimitermes/.note: The original explicitly states that the alate is unknown; for the worker only the mandibles and the fore coxa are described at genus level, the rest is reproduced as in the original, without supplementation from related genera (Coxotermes, Duplidentitermes).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate unknown. Soldier head thick and massive, the sides straight, parallel or flatly convex, with a distinct and rather deep pit between the base of the postclypeus and the opening of the frontal gland; postmentum widest behind the bases of the mandibles, constricted posteriorly; mandibles short and stout, the apices slightly hooked, each mandible with 1 small tooth slightly in front of the midpoint; lateral and posterior margins of the pronotum flared, the anterior margin broad and evenly slightly convex, without a median notch; the sharp longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa bears a long and conspicuous nipple-like process; apical spur formula 2:2:2, the outer upper surface of the fore tibia with a white circular spot. Worker with a large mandibular apical tooth, a deep incision between the first and second marginal teeth and the third marginal tooth on the left mandible, and a small second marginal tooth on the right mandible.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head thick and massive, with scattered setae, denser on the frons and the sides, a few short hairs near the fontanelle; sides straight, parallel or flatly convex; between the base of the postclypeus and the opening of the frontal gland there is a distinct and rather deep pit; the side of the head is curved in the frontal gland region and slightly bulbously swollen near the vertex. Postmentum widest behind the bases of the mandibles, the sides rounded at the widest point, becoming straight and constricted posteriorly, with a small constriction before the concave posterior margin; the lateral sutures of the postmentum are visible along the whole length except anteriorly. Postclypeus distinct, broadly hexagonal, with a clear suture separating it from the front of the head. Labrum with a white apical area, the sides of the base nearly parallel, usually curved downwards, distinctly shorter than the postclypeus, about 1/3 as wide as the postclypeus. Mandibles short and stout, the apices slightly hooked; each mandible with 1 small tooth slightly in front of the midpoint, and another small tooth at the end of the stout base projecting on the ventral surface, this tooth not continuous with the cutting edge from the apical tooth to the middle tooth but situated in front of the small molar plate, forming a somewhat independent blunt cutting edge. Lateral and posterior margins of the pronotum slightly flared, the anterior margin broad and evenly slightly convex, without a distinct notch or incision, the lateral margins rounded, the middle of the posterior margin concave and depressed. On the sharp longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa there is a very long and conspicuous nipple-like process with a rounded apex; this process is stouter and shorter than in Coxotermes, with a more concave basal face. The middle of the fore femur is as thick as in Coxotermes. Apical spur formula 2:2:2; the outer upper surface of each fore tibia bears a white circular spot, possibly the base of a reduced outer apical spur.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The principal generic characters of the mandibles are: the apical tooth is very large relative to the first marginal tooth; there is a distinct incision between the first and second marginal teeth and the third marginal tooth on the left mandible; the second marginal tooth of the right mandible is small. The sharp longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa bears a conspicuous triangular process, but not so tooth-like as in the soldier.

/genus/heterotermes/.note: The only copy of this paper available locally is the publisher's JATS full-text XML (Europe PMC PMC3264403), with no print PDF, so the locator uses section names rather than page numbers; the jsonl gives the author order as Roisin & Bourguignon, which differs from the order of the contrib elements in the XML (Bourguignon first); the XML is followed here. The worker caste is not described in the original, so no worker section is provided.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The genus is distinguished from other members of the Rhinotermitinae by the following combination: in the soldier the head is long and narrow, rectangular, the mandibles sabre-shaped with slightly curved apices, the left mandible with one tooth and several serrations at the base and the right mandible without teeth or serrations at the base; in the alate the head is almost oval, the anterior part narrower than the posterior, the ocelli situated at the front of the head, before the compound eyes, the antennae usually 15–19 segments, and the pronotum elongate and narrower than the head.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head almost oval, the anterior part narrower than the posterior; fontanelle small, situated in the middle of the head; compound eyes small and flat; ocelli situated at the front of the head, before the eyes; antennae usually 15–19 segments; pronotum elongate and narrower than the head. Species level (H. paradoxus): head slightly elongate, bearing several hundred hairs; pronotum elongate and of medium width; antennae usually 18 segments (occasionally 17); compound eyes flat, with small ocelli in front of the eyes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long and narrow, rectangular; fontanelle small, circular, situated anteriorly; labrum short to medium, about half the length of the mandibles; mandibles sabre-shaped with slightly curved apices; left mandible with one tooth and several serrations at the base; right mandible without teeth or serrations at the base; antennae 13–18 segments. Species level (H. vagus): soldier small, the head elongate with a distinct swelling anteriorly and densely covered with short hairs; labrum elongate with a sharp apex; antennae usually 13 segments; pronotum short and narrow, bearing about 50 hairs; postmentum slightly narrow and hairless; mandibular apices slightly curved.

/genus/hirsutitermes/.note: The genus-level Diagnosis lists only the three characters of the enteric valve and digestive tract; the body-wall characters are given in the genus-level Description. No soldier section (soldierless).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The posterior margin of the enteric valve armature bears several hundred fine spines; the enteric valve seating (EVS) is tubular, trilobed and long; the mesenteric tongue is long but not inflated. It is closest to Longustitermes: the spines of this genus are longer and finer than in that genus, the anterior portion of the cushions pyriform (in the latter more rounded; the original sentence reads "the anterior portion of the cushions is more rounded in the latter than pyriform in the former"); Longustitermes is smaller, with a trilobed rather than tubular EVS.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head capsule forms a very gentle curve in lateral view. Fontanelle distinct, heart-shaped, situated near the imaginary line of the posterior margins of the compound eyes, behind the oval spot (= the median labral muscle). Above the antennal sockets there are two distinct oval spots. Antennae 12-segmented, segment formula 2>3<4≈5. The median suture of the pronotum is distinct, the anterior margin raised.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic, medium-sized (body and head size from medium to large). Head capsule pale yellow, densely covered with long hairs and sparse, somewhat larger setae, flat dorsally in lateral view. Antennal segments translucent white; antennae 14-segmented, segment formula 2>3=4<5. Fontanelle circular, distinct but with indistinct margins; postclypeus moderately inflated. Pronotum with very long setae, especially numerous in the middle of the anterior and posterior lobes; the surfaces of the tergites and sternites with short hairs, the posterior margins with long setae. Fore coxa and fore femur with medium-sized spines; fore tibia moderately inflated, densely covered with spines and setae of various sizes. The apical tooth of the left mandible is more projecting than M1+2; the two margins of M3 form an obtuse angle, the apex slightly rounded and directed forwards; the molar process distinct, not concealed by the molar prominence; molar prominence well developed. The apical tooth of the right mandible is far more projecting than M1, M1 small and less projecting than M2, the margin of M2 curved; the molar plate concave, with a few ridges. Digestive tract: mesenteric tongue long but not inflated; EVS rather long and tubular, often with three small but distinct lobes; in dorsal view the junction of P3-a and the seating is visible; the armature has several hundred fine sclerotised spines, distributed from the fourth part of the distal end of the enteric valve. Measurements: species-level (Table 2).

/genus/hirtitermes/.note: Established by Holmgren 1912 and listed in the catalogue as the 1st subgenus, with only Eutermes (Hirtitermes) hirtiventris Holmgren (Sarawak). In the key the alate appears only as “(?Hirtitermes n. subg.)”, appended after the Eutermes s. str. entry, the author himself being in doubt, so no alate section is given; the original text gives no worker diagnosis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier of the Constrictus group, with a single soldier morph: nasus large, thick, conical, the depression at the nasus base large; the base of the left mandible with two distinct teeth; pilosity stiff and brown; antennal segments elongate. The contrast with Eutermes s. str. lies precisely here — the latter has the depression at the nasus base small or absent, the mandible base never toothed, the pilosity not stiff, and the antennal segments for the most part normal.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A single morph. Nasus large, thick, conical; the depression at the nasus base conspicuous, the original text noting specifically, among the characters of the group, that the depression is large in this genus; the base of the left mandible with two distinct teeth; head and nasus covered with stiff brown hairs; antennal segments long.

/genus/hoplognathotermes/.note: The alate is explicitly recorded as unknown in the original. Rewritten from the English genus diagnosis, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate unknown. Soldier: head large, sides straight and parallel; frontal gland area flat or slightly concave in section; head surface with only very few short setae near the frontal gland opening, postmentum nearly bare; each mandible with 1 conspicuous, anteriorly directed large marginal tooth situated before the midpoint, the left tooth with a long basal cutting edge; legs and fore coxae longer than in Duplidentitermes; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, middle tibia without dark outer spine.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head surface with only very few, rather short scattered setae near the frontal gland opening; fore coxa without strong spines, with only a few fine setae not forming a special arrangement; first 4 abdominal tergites with short hairs or setae, posterior tergites and sternites with additional short hairs. Head large, sides straight and parallel; frontal gland area flat or slightly concave in section. Postmentum large, moderately constricted, slightly convex in section. Antennae 15-segmented. Postclypeus distinct, slightly arched; labrum with rounded lateral margins, the sides straight and parallel behind the lateral angles, the apex rounded-obtuse. Each mandible with 1 conspicuous, large, anteriorly directed marginal tooth situated before the midpoint; left tooth with a long basal cutting edge (unlike Firmitermes). Pronotum with a larger anterior lobe, the median notch of the anterior margin shallow and indistinct. Legs longer than in Duplidentitermes; fore coxa also longer, simple, the longitudinal ridge obtuse and unspecialised, straight or flatly convex in section, extending about 1/3–1/2 from the apex towards the base, convex between ridge and inner margin. Femora slender, nearly equally thick at the middle. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2, middle tibia without dark outer spine.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Apical teeth of both mandibles only slightly larger than the first marginal tooth; cutting edges of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible long and less undulating (straighter than in Duplidentitermes and other closely related genera of the subfamily); a distinct notch between the first and second marginal teeth and the third marginal tooth; compared with Acutidentitermes, the first marginal teeth of both mandibles less anteriorly directed, the angle between apical tooth and first marginal tooth more obtuse, the cutting edges of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible proportionally slightly shorter.

/genus/humutermes/.note: The only genus-level measurement is the worker head width 0.49–0.62 mm; the other measurements are species-level. No soldier section (soldierless). Along with Patawatermes and Rubeotermes, this genus comes from the same paper, Bourguignon & Roisin (2016); the three sources are merged into a single record.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The mixed segment of the worker is elongate, its inner end inflated into a white spherical mesenteric diverticulum; this character is shared with Anoplotermes sensu stricto and distinguishes the genus from the remaining South American soldierless termite genera. The main difference from Anoplotermes s.s. lies in the enteric valve: the enteric valve of this genus consists of 6 pads, each with 10–20 long spines extending into the paunch (P3); the fontanelle of the alate is larger and more elongate.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes and ocelli medium-sized. Fontanelle medium-sized, appearing as an elongate white spot between the two eyes. Pronotum semicircular in dorsal view, with several hundred small setae and several tens of long setae. The posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum slightly concave, the angles rounded.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Very small to small, head width 0.49–0.62 mm (genus-level measurement). Head capsule white, covered with more than 100 small setae. Fontanelle almost invisible. Fore tibia inflated at the middle. Digestive tract very similar to that of Anoplotermes sensu stricto: the midgut and proctodeum overlap, forming a distinct long mixed segment whose mesenteric part is inflated at its inner end into a white spherical diverticulum. The enteric valve is inserted into the extension of the paunch and consists of 6 sclerotised pads with a well-developed sclerotised armature.

/genus/labiotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, p. 50). The original established it as a subgenus of Cornitermes (Untergattung Labiotermes n. subg.), the generic characters being those of the subgenus, and further subdivided it into two groups (Sektion 1/2); no separate genus-level diagnosis is given in the text, so the 'Diagnostic characters' section is based on the subgeneric characters and the differences between the two groups.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Holmgren 1912 established Labiotermes as a new subgenus within Cornitermes. The alate has large compound eyes and large ocelli set close against them, antennae of 17 segments, and mandibular tooth 1 larger than tooth 2; the soldier has a relatively short frontal tube, a long labrum with a transparent, sharply delimited tip, antennae of 13–15 segments, and at most 2 teeth in the middle of the left mandible; the worker has antennae of 14–15 (16) segments and mandibular tooth 1 longer than tooth 2. The original text further divides the group into two: one with soldier antennae of 15 segments, the left mandible bearing 2 middle teeth and the basal and middle teeth of the right mandible separate; the other with the alate unknown, soldier antennae of 13 segments, the left mandible without middle teeth and the basal and middle teeth of the right mandible fused.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes large; ocelli large, very close to the compound eyes. Antennae of 17 segments. Mandibular tooth 1 larger than tooth 2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Frontal tube relatively short. Labrum long, with a sharply delimited transparent tip. Mandibles robust; left mandible with at most 2 teeth in the middle. Antennae of 13–15 segments.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae of 14–15 (16) segments. Mandibular tooth 1 longer than tooth 2. The original text gives only these two diagnostic features for the worker of this subgenus and does not describe the rest separately (it still falls within the generic characters of Cornitermes).

/genus/lacessititermes/.note: Established by Holmgren 1912 and listed in the catalogue as the 18th subgenus, noted for the East Indies, with the species alipes, atrior, breviarticulatus, filicornis, laborator, lacessitiformis, lacessitus, piliferus and others (including new species). The original text has only key entries and no worker diagnosis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier nasus relatively narrowly conical, antennae 14-segmented, head often constricted, antennal segment 3 shorter than segment 4; in the same group Longipeditermes has segment 3 equal to or longer than segment 4, two soldier morphs and one distinct tooth at the mandible apex, while Hospitalitermes is monomorphic and has no tooth at the mandible apex. Alate clypeus shorter than half its width, only very slightly paler than the frons or concolorous with it, the frons behind the clypeus with a triangular depression, body and wings dark, antennal segment 3 slightly longer than segment 2, fontanelle indistinct and slit-like — distinguished from Hospitalitermes (segment 3 twice as long as segment 2, fontanelle distinct, oval, whitish).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Clypeus shorter than half its width, only (very) slightly paler than the frons or concolorous with it; frons with a triangular depression behind the clypeus; body dark, wings dark; antennal segment 3 slightly longer than segment 2; fontanelle indistinct, slit-like.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Nasus relatively narrowly conical; antennae 14-segmented; head often constricted; antennal segment 3 shorter than segment 4; body mostly dark, legs long.

/genus/leptomyxotermes/.note: The genus name derives from the Greek leptos (slender) and myxa (lamp spout, jug spout). The 1965 generic diagnosis by Sands contains two sections, imago and Soldier, and no worker section. The original text notes that the small tooth connecting the molar prominence with the 3rd marginal tooth is reduced and set back in this genus, whereas it is visible in Fulleritermes and Rhadinotermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands established this genus for the African forest species doriae, which had previously been placed, together with Rhadinotermes, in Coarctotermes. Alate: the cutting edge before the 3rd marginal tooth of the left mandible has a distinct notch, a feature shared with Rhadinotermes and Fulleritermes; but in this genus the compound eyes and ocelli are very large and prominent, the fontanelle is slit-like and does not clearly fork anteriorly, and the molar plate of the right mandible has only 6–7 ridges (7–9 in Fulleritermes, 13–14 in Grallatotermes). Soldier monomorphic with traces of a second morph, nasus columnar, head strongly constricted behind the antennae, antennae 14-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Apical tooth of the left mandible as long as the 1st marginal tooth, the distance from the apical tooth to the 1st marginal tooth half the distance between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth (left mandible index about 50); the cutting edge between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth with a distinct concavity in front of the 3rd marginal tooth. Apical tooth of the right mandible nearly as long as the 1st marginal tooth, the posterior cutting edge of the 1st marginal tooth about as long as that of the 2nd marginal tooth, the latter distinctly concave; surface of the molar plate with a notch on the anterior margin near the base, the posterior margin extended into a rounded wing, the 1st molar ridge tooth-like, the remaining 6–7 diminishing towards the base. Fontanelle slit-like, not clearly forking anteriorly. Compound eyes and ocelli very large and prominent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A single morph, with traces of a second morph. Nasus columnar. Reduced mandibles with a small point. Head capsule strongly constricted behind the antennae. Antennae 14-segmented.

/genus/longipeditermes/.note: Established by Holmgren 1912 and listed in the catalogue as the 16th subgenus, with only Eutermes (Longipeditermes) longipes Haviland (Malacca and Borneo). In the key the alate appears only as “(?Longipeditermes n. subg.)”, appended after the Hospitalitermes entry, the author being in doubt, so no alate section is given; the original text gives no worker diagnosis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier dimorphic, a point specially marked in the key (most other genera of the group being monomorphic); nasus relatively narrowly conical, antennae 14-segmented, head often constricted, mandible apex with only one distinct tooth, antennal segment 3 equal to or longer than segment 4. Lacessititermes has segment 3 shorter than segment 4 and is monomorphic; Hospitalitermes is monomorphic and has no tooth at the mandible apex.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier dimorphic. Nasus relatively narrowly conical; antennae 14-segmented; head often constricted; mandible apex with one distinct tooth; antennal segment 3 equal to or longer than segment 4; legs long.

/genus/mastotermes/.note: The paper is a family-level taxonomic revision; the generic morphology is concentrated in the wing venation, and the original has no sections on soldier or worker morphology, so only diagnostic characters and the alate are given. Two points are easily misattributed: the archidictyon reticulate venation (the original states explicitly that it is shared by the Mastotermitidae and the Hodotermitidae and is not a generic character); and the media joining the radial sector a short distance behind the humeral suture, which is a general feature of termites (the original says 'in nearly all cases'); neither is included.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Generic characters at the level of the wing venation: the radial sector of the forewing is strongly fused, with the adjacent upper branches closely spaced; the humeral suture of the forewing is more curved and more convex than in Blattotermes; the hindwing has a well-developed anal lobe, which the original describes as a feature of this genus and its close relatives; the radial sector is compact and the media lies closer to the radial sector and farther from the anterior cubitus, on which basis wing-only specimens can be assigned to this genus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The radial sector of the forewing is highly fused, with the adjacent upper branches closely spaced; the humeral suture of the forewing forms a distinct arcuate convexity and is more curved than in Blattotermes; the anal lobe of the hindwing is well developed.

/genus/mimeutermes/.note: Established by Silvestri 1914, type species Mimeutermes giffardii. Sands 1965 records three species and considers that the genus evolved in the West African rain forest. All three sections are taken from the original generic diagnosis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands places this genus in the Paracornitermes group of the Ethiopian region. Alate: apical tooth of the left mandible long, the cutting edge between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth short and slightly concave (left mandible index 2.00–2.23), the gap between the 3rd marginal tooth and the molar plate less than half the width of that cutting edge; 2nd marginal tooth of the right mandible absent, the molar plate with prominent anterior and posterior rounded wings, tapering towards the apex, without ridges — the absence of ridges makes it easy to distinguish from Fulleritermes, Leptomyxotermes, Grallatotermes and other ridged genera. Soldier monomorphic, nasus thickly conical, joining the tapering base of the head capsule, head in dorsal view not constricted, top-shaped together with the nasus, antennae 12-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Left mandible with a long apical tooth, the cutting edge between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth short and slightly concave (left mandible index 2.00–2.23), the gap between the 3rd marginal tooth and the molar plate less than half the width of that cutting edge. Apical tooth and 1st marginal tooth of the right mandible as in the left mandible, 2nd marginal tooth absent, the posterior cutting edge of the 1st marginal tooth concave, the molar plate with prominent anterior and posterior rounded wings, tapering towards the apex, without ridges. Postclypeus slightly raised, twice as wide as long or a little less. Fontanelle pale, slit-like, slightly forking anteriorly and with a pale spot, or nearly obsolete, only slightly paler than the head. Compound eyes slightly projecting from the sides of the head. Head pilosity variable. Posterior margin of the pronotum rounded, anterior margin concave.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A single morph. Nasus thickly conical, its base joining the taper of the head capsule, fontanelle relatively large. Reduced mandibles pointed or unpointed; anterior margin of the labrum undulate. Head capsule in dorsal view not constricted, top-shaped together with the nasus, sides parallel or rounded posteriorly. Antennae 12-segmented. Head and nasus with only a few conspicuous setae. Tergite hairs sparse, scattered and minute, those of the posterior margin and of the last 2–3 tergites longer; sternite hairs sparse and short, those of the posterior margin about twice as long as the short hairs.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibles as in the alate, only the apical tooth proportionally longer (left mandible index 3.32–3.59) and the molar plate of the right mandible larger with more prominent wings.

/genus/mycterotermes/.note: Sands 1965 explicitly records Imago: Unknown, hence only a soldier section. The original text notes that the genus was established on material from Sia Ding alone, a monotypic genus with a single species; its diagnostic characters share much with the Neotropical Diversitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands established this genus for meringocephalus from Sia Ding, considering it close to Trinervitermes but more primitive, possibly even the ancestor of the latter, its diagnostic characters having much in common with the Neotropical Diversitermes. Soldier dimorphic: the major soldier has a short, columnar nasus and the head very weakly constricted behind the antennae; the minor soldier has a weakly conical nasus and a more evident constriction of the head; the antennae are possibly 13-segmented in the major soldier and 12-segmented in the minor. Alate unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic. Major soldier: nasus short, columnar, reduced mandibles with a small but distinct point showing traces of the marginal and apical teeth; head capsule very weakly constricted behind the antennae, vertex and nasus with short, conspicuous bristle-like hairs. Minor soldier: identical to the major soldier except for the weakly conical nasus and the more evident constriction of the head capsule behind the antennae. Antennae possibly 13-segmented in the major soldier and 12-segmented in the minor.

/genus/occasitermes/.note: The original text has only the subgeneric key and no genus-level Diagnosis; the above are the key couplets, and measurements, body colour and worker are all not given. Holmgren (p. 68), on the basis of its long, thick nasus and the alate characters of the Subulitermes group, regards the genus as a relatively primitive member of that group and suggests that it is rather closely related to Tumulitermes. The genus name is given in the original text as a new subgenus (n. subg.).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among Holmgren's subgenera of Eutermes, the soldier is characterised by the combination of mandibles entirely without an apical process, a long and thick nasus, 12-segmented antennae, and a head capsule not constricted behind the antennal sockets; Eutermellus of the same group has only a weak constriction behind the antennal sockets and can be separated further by head and nasus shape. In the key the alate falls in the Subulitermes group: 1st tooth of the left mandible distinctly larger than the 2nd, fontanelle about at the middle of the head, antennal segments relatively long, pronotum narrow. In his systematic discussion Holmgren points out in particular that the alate belongs to the Subulitermes group while the soldier has a long, thick nasus (similar to that of Rhynchotermes), so he regards the genus as a key member of that branch retaining primitive characters; but what he gives are only key characters, not a complete genus-level description.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, usually narrowing anteriorly; fontanelle about at the middle of the head; antennal segments relatively long; pronotum narrow (Taf. III, Fig. 7). The couplets leading to this genus in the key also include: clypeus usually about as long as half its width, or shorter and rather strongly raised, oval, pale yellow; 1st tooth of the left mandible distinctly larger than the 2nd. Wing surface pilosity and venation are not delimited in the key in the original text, only compared through the plate.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles without an apical process; the species are small, antennae 11–12-segmented, 12-segmented in this genus; nasus conical, long and thick; frontal profile straight (compared in the key with Taf. III, Fig. 17); head capsule not constricted behind the antennal sockets.

/genus/orthognathotermes/.note: Alate unknown; from the nymph the original records 17-segmented antennae, a postclypeal basis slightly shorter than half its width, and a large first mandibular tooth. The German genus diagnosis is rewritten from OCR text, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate unknown (nymph with 17-segmented antennae). Soldier: head rectangular, rather flatly convex, frons flat; frontal prominence and fontanelle both absent; above the antennal socket a rather large, rounded-obtuse, tubercle-like widening of the antennal ridge; labrum short, about as long as wide, lingulate but with the lateral angles projecting slightly rounded-obtusely (weakly trilobed); mandibles symmetrical, with a median tooth at the middle; antennae 15-segmented; pronotum saddle-shaped.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular, rather flatly convex, frons flat; frontal prominence and fontanelle both absent; above the antennal socket a rather large, rounded-obtuse, tubercle-like widening of the antennal ridge. Labrum short, about as long as wide, lingulate, but with the lateral angles projecting slightly rounded-obtusely (weakly trilobed). Mandibles symmetrical; base very wide, passing forwards over a rather long stretch into the middle of the mandible, with a trace of a tooth at the transition between base and middle; mandible slightly geniculate-bent outwards before the midpoint, the bend forming the median tooth; apex curved inwards; upper surface of the right mandibular apex slightly concave. Antennae 15-segmented. Pronotum saddle-shaped.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Postclypeus about as long as half its width, arched; first mandibular tooth large; antennae 14-segmented.

/genus/patawatermes/.note: Genus-level measurements: worker head width 0.69–1.1 mm. Soldierless. The page numbers of the genus-level treatment could not be verified from the Zenodo record (the record gives only the isPartOf full text and the author order), so the locator gives only the genus-level treatment and the author-year.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Very similar to Grigiotermes, but clearly distinguishable by the shape of the enteric valve armature of the worker; moreover, although the worker P1 is swollen, it is less so than in Grigiotermes. The same set of morphological criteria (integument, mandibles, digestive tract and enteric valve) also separates the genus from the remaining South American soldierless termite genera.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Sclerotised parts dark brown, densely covered with several thousand minute setae. Head capsule with about 100 sparse long setae. Compound eyes and ocelli large. Fontanelle small to medium-sized, situated at the level of the anterior margin of the compound eyes. Pronotum elongate, with several dozen long setae. Posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum slightly concave, angles strongly rounded.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Medium to large, head width 0.69–1.1 mm (genus-level measurements). Head capsule pale yellow, rounded, scattered with minute setae and about 100 long setae; fontanelle small, almost indistinct; mandibles and protibia as in figures 5C and 5D of the original. Enteric valve inserted into the tubular extension of the paunch, armature well developed, consisting of 6 circular spiny pads; anterior part of the enteric valve consisting of 6 oval cushions, each composed of about 50–80 scales, with a fringe of spines on the posterior margin. The mesenteron–proctodeum junction forms a small bulb, covered by the proctodeum, slightly elongated into a short, distinct mixed segment; hindgut P1 wide.

/genus/porotermes/.note: The usable generic characters are concentrated in the key to the genera of the subfamily and the comparison on p. 144; body length, number of antennal segments and pronotal proportions are species-level measurements of P. adamsoni and are marked as species level. The worker section is the original's statement about the caste in the subfamily and is not peculiar to this genus; that qualification must be retained when citing it.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The key to the genera of the subfamily given in the original: an alate without ocelli, without an empodium (the pad between the claws) and with 5-segmented cerci belongs to this genus, whereas one with ocelli, with an empodium and with 2-segmented cerci belongs to Calotermes; a soldier with long, 5-segmented cerci belongs to this genus, and one with short, 2-segmented cerci to Calotermes. The soldier is easily confused with Stolotermes, but the latter is smaller, with a flatter head and body, a small heart-shaped pronotum, and eyes bearing ommatidia.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Ocelli absent; empodium absent; cerci 5-segmented. Species level (P. adamsoni): antennae 15 to 17 segments; body length with wings 14–15 mm, body length 7–8 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Cerci long, 5-segmented. Species level (P. adamsoni): antennae 16 to 18 segments; mandibles stout, the tooth formula the same in the three species; pronotum about 1.5 times as wide as the head.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The subfamily has no true worker caste; the worker function is performed by immature stages of the alate (and possibly of the soldier); the generic characters of this worker-nymph are the same as those of the soldier.

/genus/postsubulitermes/.note: The alate is taken mainly from Sands's generic characters (the mandibles of his queen specimen were not dissected, hence the absence of mandibular characters), and Emerson's original description supplements the pilosity, head shape, pronotum and meso- and metanotal characters. The soldier and worker sections combine Sands and Emerson, without separate annotation where the two agree; the measurements are those of Emerson. Sands considered the genus close to Afrosubulitermes, the evenly rounded margin of the soldier labrum being a further reduction of the trilobed labrum of Eutermellus.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Established by Emerson 1960 and supplemented by Sands 1965: the soldier is monomorphic, the nasus slenderly cylindrical, tapering forwards to a fine point, the mandibles without a point, the anterior margin of the labrum evenly rounded, the head capsule hardly constricted behind the antennal fossae and slightly raised at the base of the nasus, the antennae 12-segmented, the setae very few (a pair on the dorsum of the head, one to two pairs at the base of the nasus, a few at its tip); in the alate the postclypeus is moderately arched, twice as wide as long, its anterior margin wavy and convex in the middle, the fontanelle a long Y, the compound eyes not projecting beyond the sides of the head, the pilosity extremely fine and sparse (3 hairs on each eye, 2 pairs on the vertex, 1 pair on the postclypeus), the lateral margins of the pronotum contracted posteriorly, whose length is less than two-thirds of its width; in the worker the apical tooth of the left mandible is much longer than the first marginal tooth (index 2.63), the cutting edge between the first and third marginal teeth is entire and concave, the gap between the third marginal tooth and the molar process is extremely narrow, the second marginal tooth of the right mandible is missing, and the molar plate has a weak basal concavity, a weak anterior and a strong rounded posterior ridge, and no transverse ridges. Emerson adds: the head is dark brown and the pronotum yellow, in striking contrast; the soldier head is 1.39–1.53 mm long and 0.55–0.60 mm wide, the pronotum 0.34–0.39 mm, the hind tibia 0.71–0.79 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head and postclypeus bear sparse short hairs and several long setae; the pronotum bears several long setae near its lateral and posterior margins and a few short hairs on its surface; the abdominal tergites and sternites both bear numerous long setae or hairs of nearly equal length. The ocelli are large and distinct, separated from the compound eyes by less than half their width, slightly larger than the antennal fossae. The fontanelle is pale brown, elongate, forked at its end, set in a shallow depression on the vertex. The postclypeus is about half as long as wide (0.18 mm × 0.36 mm). The lateral margins of the pronotum are fairly straight and contracted posteriorly, the posterior angles rounded, the posterior margin slightly concave; the posterior angles of the mesonotum are slightly less than a right angle and its median concavity slightly greater than a right angle; the posterior angles of the metanotum are more rounded, about equal to a right angle, and its median concavity greater than that of the mesonotum. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. The antennae of the specimen are broken off.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Setae and short hairs are scattered over the face of the head; there are several hairs at the tip of the frontal projection but no short hairs in the middle or at its base. The pronotum bears a few short hairs, more numerous anteriorly. Each abdominal tergite bears a row of posterior marginal setae and scattered hairs about one-third their length; the setae and hairs of the sternites are both longer than those of the tergites, the hairs about half as long as the setae. The head is oval in dorsal view, the frontal projection slender and slightly tapering forwards, a slight constriction visible behind the antennal fossae (both in dorsal and in lateral view). Antennae 12-segmented. The mandibles are without a point. The anterior margin of the pronotum is very shallowly and indistinctly concave. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. The head is dark brown and the pronotum yellow, in striking contrast.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The apical tooth of the mandibles is proportionally longer than in Afrosubulitermes and Verrucositermes; in the left mandible the third marginal tooth is indistinct, the cutting edge between the first and third marginal teeth is entire and concave, and the gap between the third marginal tooth and the molar process is extremely narrow; in the right mandible the second marginal tooth is missing, the molar plate has a weak concavity near the base, the anterior ridge weak and the posterior ridge strong and rounded, and there are no transverse ridges. Left mandibular index 2.63.

/genus/procapritermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, p. 113). The list of four species is on the same page: atypus n. sp., minutus Hav. and setiger Hav., all from Borneo; the discussion of systematic relationships begins in the lower part of p. 113 (the author states that this genus is in fact formed by slight differentiation from the Protocapritermes subgenus of Mirotermes). zh_name provisionally uses the Latin name (marked '—' in the batch).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A new genus established by Holmgren 1912, containing 3 species, all from Borneo: Procapritermes atypus (new species), P. minutus (Hav.) and P. setiger (Hav.). The alate has antennae of 14 segments, markedly incrassate towards the apex, the last segment bearing a pointed appendage at its tip; the soldier has a long rectangular head without a frontal projection, the mandibles slender and asymmetric, their curvature of the same type as in Capritermes but very weak, with a sharp, strong tooth above the basal segment; the worker has a rather small, broadly oval head, mandibles with a large apical tooth, and antennae of 14 segments. The original text notes that this genus is in fact a genus formed by slight differentiation from the Protocapritermes subgenus of Mirotermes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, narrowed anteriorly. Compound eyes relatively small. Ocelli separated from the compound eyes by hardly more than their diameter. Clypeal base shorter than half its width, flatly convex, without a median line. Mandibular tooth 1 large. Antennae of 14 segments, markedly incrassate towards the apex, the last segment with a pointed appendage at its tip. Posterior parts of the meso- and metanotum narrowed, with an emargination at the end. Wing membrane with fine punctures (spines). Media close to the cubitus. Abdomen slender. Without styli.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head slender, rectangular, without a frontal projection, relatively flat, truncate progressively anteriorly. Frontal gland opening small, fully visible from above, surrounded by sparse hairs (a vestigial hair ring). Clypeal base very narrow, bounded by the large mandibular basal segments. Labrum much longer than wide, either symmetrical or distinctly deflected to the right. Mandibles slender and asymmetric, the outer basal margin of the left mandible fairly strongly concave; their curvature of the same type as in Capritermes, but only very weakly expressed. A sharp, strong tooth above the basal segment. Antennae of 14 segments, segment 3 longer than segment 2 and about as long as segment 4. Pronotum small, saddle-shaped.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head rather small, broadly oval. Clypeal base with a very weakly convex posterior margin and a straight anterior margin, shorter (much shorter) than half its width, fairly strongly convex. Mandibles with a large apical tooth. Antennae of 14 segments. Pronotum small, saddle-shaped.

/genus/prohamitermes/.note: Published in the original as a new genus (n. g.), with diagnoses for all three castes. The German genus diagnosis is rewritten, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate, soldier and worker all known. Alate: head broadly oval, compound eyes large and flatly convex, not projecting, ocelli level with the frontal surface, fontanelle distinct and rather far back, postclypeal basis far shorter than half its width; antennae 15-segmented. Soldier: head oval, slightly narrowing anteriorly, eyeless, fontanelle very weak, labrum nearly triangular without a hyaline apical point, mandibles sickle-curved with 2 small teeth on each side at the middle, submentum strongly humped at the middle; antennae 14-segmented; fore tibia with 3 spurs, meso- and metatibia with 2 each. Worker: postclypeal basis lenticular, rather strongly arched, antennae 14-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head (rather) broad, oval, slightly longer than wide; compound eyes rather large, flatly convex, not projecting; ocelli level with the frontal surface (inner margin not raised), distance to the compound eye less than their diameter; fontanelle distinct, rather far back. Postclypeal basis far shorter than half its width, posterior margin only slightly convex, anterior margin straight, nearly flat. Labrum at the middle wider than at the base, without a chitinous transverse band. Mandibles with the Termes-type armature, base not excessively projecting. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 shorter than segment 2 and as long as segment 4. Pronotum small, saddle very weak, anterior margin straight; emargination of the posterior margin of the mesonotum wider than that of the metanotum; posterior angles rounded. Forewing scale slightly longer than the hindwing scale; wings covered with fine hairs; in the forewing the media arises directly from the wing scale, in the hindwing the media arises from the radial sector. Cerci short, without styli; dealate individual no larger than the soldier; lateral margins of the female abdomen finely and densely longitudinally wrinkled; glandular setae rather sparse in both sexes; apical spur 3 of the tibia reduced.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head oval, slightly narrowing anteriorly, flatly convex, flattening anteriorly towards the labrum; eyeless; cranial sutures invisible. Fontanelle very weak, about the middle of the head; fontanelle gland small. Postclypeus short and flat. Labrum nearly triangular, without a hyaline apical point. Mandibles sickle-curved, sharply pointed, base large, middle rather short, apex long, its base slightly tooth-like widened; each side of the middle with 2 small teeth; each side of the base with 1 small, rather wide molar prominence. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 only slightly longer than segment 2, segment 2 slightly longer than segment 4. Submentum strongly humped (or bullate) at the middle. Pronotum rather small, upfolded in a very strong saddle (almost a right angle), anterior lobe as long as the posterior part; cerci short, without styli. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, meso- and metatibia with 2 each.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head oval, widest at the antennae; fontanelle rather far back. Postclypeal basis lenticular, shorter than half its width, rather strongly arched. Toothed inner margin of the left mandible shortened, molar region strongly projecting, roughly as in Hamitermes. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 2 as long as segment 3 and slightly longer than segment 4. Pronotum with a strong saddle, anterior lobe longer than the posterior part.

/genus/protermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 24–26). The original divides the genus into the two subgenera Allodontermes and Protermes s. str.; the alate paragraph describes only the subgenus Allodontermes (end of p. 24–p. 25), the soldier paragraph treats both subgenera together, the two forms of labrum and left mandible being distinguished by figs 7 and 8; the lists of subgenera and species are not included in the description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Holmgren 1912 divided the genus into the two subgenera Allodontermes and Protermes s. str., 3 species being known at the time, all from Africa. Alate antennae 19 segments; soldier antennae 14–17 segments; worker antennae 16–17 segments. Worker compound eyes either reduced or very distinct and even pigmented; pronotum very small, less than half the head width, anterior lobe upturned. The apex of the labrum and the tooth-like expansion at the apex of the left mandible differ between the two subgenera (shown in figs 7 and 8 of the original).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: This paragraph is headed Allodontermes in the original and reads as follows. Head broadly oval. Compound eyes large, strongly projecting. Ocelli broadly oval, lateral, very close to the compound eyes; spiral in dorsal view, frons flat and depressed. Frontal gland opening small, bright. Base of clypeus bright, rather strongly arched, at least as long as half its width, posterior margin strongly convexly curved, anterior margin straight, the sides reaching the mandibular bases; apex relatively well developed. Labrum longer than broad, narrowing slightly anteriorly, with a narrow transverse chitinous band in the middle. Left mandible with typical Termes-type dentition; right mandible deviating from the Termes type, with a much reduced second tooth, transitional from the Leucotermes type to the Termes type. Antennae 19 segments, third segment shorter than the second and fourth, fourth slightly shorter than the second. Pronotum about as long as half its width, slightly narrower than the head with the mandibles, flat; meso- and metanotum broadly incised. Forewing scale distinctly larger than the hindwing scale, but not reaching the base of the latter. Radius rather weak, soon merging with the anterior wing margin; radial sector reaching the wing apex; media of forewing separate from the wing scale, media of hindwing departing from the base of the radial sector, the media of both wings close to the cubitus and more or less branched towards the apex. Cubitus many-branched, wing membrane hyaline, slightly reticulate. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs. Cerci short; male with a stylus, female with exudatory hairs.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head parallel, both ends very weakly narrowing, flattened and arched. Frontal gland opening very indistinct, frontal gland small. Clypeus relatively short, projecting slightly anteriorly, mandibular bases very stout. Labrum in the Allodontermes form (fig. 7) longer, apex sharp and hyaline, in the Protermes form (fig. 8) relatively short, apex rounded. Apex of the left mandible with a tooth-like expansion at its base, with or without a very small tooth tubercle; left mandible with 3 more or less distinct teeth; right mandible with a large tooth before the middle, sometimes with a reduced tooth between this tooth and the apex. Antennae 14–17 segments, second segment longer than the third. Postmentum with parallel sides.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head relatively large, parallel-sided oval, flattened and arched. Frontal gland opening indistinct, head sutures not visible. Base of clypeus rather arched, transversely oval, rather large, not quite reaching the mandibular bases. Compound eyes either reduced or very distinct and even pigmented; mandibular bases very large, right mandible with traces of a second tooth. Antennae 16–17 segments, second segment longer than the third, third segment equal to or slightly longer than the fourth. Pronotum small, less than half the head width, with an upturned anterior lobe. At least the fore and mid tibiae with lateral spines, fore tibia with 3 apical spurs. Styli present.

/genus/protohamitermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 77–78). The original explicitly writes 'Soldat unbekannt' (soldier unknown), so only the alate and worker sections are given; the worker section begins on the last line of p. 77 and continues on the first line of p. 78. The original describes a new genus and species, Protohamitermes globiceps n. sp.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A monotypic genus, with only the species globiceps, from Sarawak, Borneo. The left mandible has the Leucotermes-type dentition (4 teeth before the basal segment), on which basis Holmgren placed the genus in the Hamitermes branch and considered its position in that branch fairly primitive. The alate is brown and densely hairy, the wings fairly short and hairy; antennae of 14 segments; worker antennae of 13 segments. Soldier unknown.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Brown, densely hairy, the wings fairly short and hairy. Head very strongly broadly convex, slightly depressed around the frontal gland opening. Compound eyes medium-sized, fairly strongly convex; ocelli relatively small, separated from the compound eyes by more than one eye diameter. Frontal gland opening behind the middle of the head, large, dark. Clypeal base very short and flat, without a longitudinal line, the apical piece large. Left mandible with the Leucotermes-type dentition, 4 teeth before the basal segment; right mandible with only 3 anterior teeth, of which the apical is far shorter than the others. Antennae of 14 segments, segment 3 small. Pronotum narrower than the head; the emargination of the posterior margin of the mesonotum wider than that of the metanotum. Forewing scale slightly larger than the hindwing scale; media with 1–2 apical branches, cubitus with 12–18 branches; all veins distinct, the inner 5–7 thickened. Cerci thick and short; without styli; tarsi short.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Densely hairy and setose. Head round, sometimes even wider than long, thick, slightly depressed in the middle. Frontal gland opening large, sometimes dark. Clypeal base short and flat. Mandibular basal segments large, mandibles as in the alate. Antennae of 13 segments, fairly thick, segment 3 shorter than segment 2 and segment 4 longer than segment 3. Pronotum short, saddle-shaped, the anterior margin not concave. Cerci short and thick, without styli. Tarsi short. Abdomen thick.

/genus/psammotermes/.note: The original publication of the genus (Desneux 1902, Saharan material) is held locally only as a 403 page with no text and cannot be used; all the characters given here come from the genus-level comparison made by Emerson (1950) when describing Glossotermes, cover only the soldier and do not include the alate or the worker; reliability is moderate. The account must not be extended to other castes on this basis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Comparison with Glossotermes brings out the soldier characters of this genus: head and body with numerous long hairs; mandibles more curved, both with coarse serrations at mid-length; left mandible without an inner groove at the base, the basal part proportionally larger and the apical part smaller; the suture between the postclypeus and the frons indistinct; labrum large and broad, without a transverse pale band, the apex sharper and without a hyaline margin; postmentum relatively broader at its narrowest point; eye spots indistinct; more antennal segments; anterior margin of the pronotum without lobe-like processes; femora stouter; tibial spur formula 3:2:2. On this basis the original considers the soldier of this genus more primitive in its mandibles, antennae and tibial spur formula.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The soldier bears numerous long hairs all over; mandibles curved, both with coarse serrations at mid-length; left mandible without an inner groove at the base; labrum large and broad, the apex pointed, without a hyaline margin; antennal segments more numerous; anterior margin of the pronotum without lobe-like processes; femora stout; tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

/genus/pseudomicrotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 126–127). The lower half of p. 127 is a point-by-point comparison of Pseudomicrotermes and Microtermes together with a discussion of systematic relationships; only the generic-character paragraphs were used here. The original work places this genus under the 'Pseudomicrotermes-Reihe'; the Chinese name for the genus was assigned by the batch.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A new genus established by Holmgren 1912, with the single species Pseudomicrotermes alboniger (Wasm.) from the Congo; a synonym in part of Mirotermes (Wasmann 1911). Originally placed in Microtermes, it was separated because morphological examination showed only a habit-based resemblance to Microtermes; according to Holmgren's comparative table, the alate of this genus is 'very small', with a very large head far wider than the pronotum, and the soldier head is rectangular and much longer than wide, differing from Microtermes in the relative length of the clypeal base, the length-to-width ratio of the labrum, the mandibular dentition and the wing venation (presence or absence of an accessory vein, reticulation). The soldier labrum is lanceolate, more than twice as long as wide; the mandibles are sabre-shaped and curved, the outer basal margin not concave; antennae of 13–14 segments; cerci unusually long, without styli.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Very small in size. Head very large, fairly strongly convex, thick, slightly narrowed anteriorly. Compound eyes medium-sized, flat. Ocelli small, separated from the compound eyes by hardly more than their diameter, facing fully laterally, their inner margin slightly raised. Frontal gland opening far back, with a dark spot in the middle. Transverse band very long. Clypeal base short, much shorter than half its width, slightly convex, posterior margin slightly concave, anterior margin straight. Labrum about as wide as long. Apical tooth of the mandibles slightly swollen. Antennae of 16 segments, incrassate towards the apex. Pronotum rather small, the anterior lobe incurved with a concave anterior margin; posterior margin concave. Posterior parts of the meso- and metanotum slightly pointed, with a rectangular emargination. Forewing scale slightly larger than the hindwing scale. Wing membrane transparent, with extremely fine punctures, without reticulation; veins very indistinct; media close to the cubitus, apparently only very weakly branched (simple?); cubitus with about 10 branches. Abdomen white. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with only 2. The 2nd tarsomere counted from the apex extended into a slender projection. Cerci fairly long. Without styli.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular with rounded corners, much longer than wide, thick. Frons slightly inclined. Frontal gland opening on the horizontal part of the head, near the edge of the inclined part. Labrum lanceolate, more than twice as long as wide, with a small transparent tip behind which a few setae arise. Mandibles sabre-shaped and curved, the outer basal margin not concave. Left mandible with a bilobed basal tooth and three very small but sharp teeth in the middle; the apex weak, microscopically serrate. Right mandible with two small teeth at the base and only a tooth-like blunt swelling in the middle. Antennae of 13–14 segments, incrassate towards the apex. Pronotum small, saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe large with a deeply concave anterior margin. Cerci unusually long. Without styli.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head broadly oval, longer than wide. Frontal gland opening fairly far back. Clypeal base slightly shorter than half its width, posterior margin fairly strongly convex, anterior margin slightly concave. Mandibles as in the alate. Antennae of 15–16 segments. Pronotum saddle-shaped, the anterior margin deeply concave. Cerci long. Without styli.

/genus/rhadinotermes/.note: The generic characters are taken from Sands's genus-level Diagnosis; the body colour, indices and measurements are taken from his subsequent description of the species R. coarctatus and have been incorporated and identified as species-level data. The original genus-level diagnosis has only Imago and Soldier sections and no Worker section, so no worker section is given. Sands notes that the genus was separated from Coarctotermes, the soldiers of the two being similar but their phylogenetic positions different.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands placed the genus in the Procornitermes branch; the soldier head capsule is sharply constricted behind the antennal fossae, resembling Fulleritermes, but phylogenetically it is not close to Leptomyxotermes/Grallatotermes, belonging instead to a predominantly Neotropical clade containing Velocitermes, Tenuirostritermes and Diversitermes; its former placement in Coarctotermes was based only on soldier similarity. The soldier is monomorphic, the nasus conical, the mandibles with a small point, the posterior lobe usually only about a quarter wider than the anterior part, the antennae 12-segmented; in the alate the left mandibular index is 0.32–0.36, the second marginal tooth is absent, the right molar plate bears 6–7 transverse ridges diminishing towards the base, the first forming a coarse tooth, and the fontanelle is a very narrow slit, hardly forked anteriorly. The generic name derives from the Greek rhadinos (tapering).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule very dark brown to pitch black, the postclypeus and antennae dark sepia-brown, the wings semitransparent pale brown; the posterior margin of the head behind the compound eyes is almost semicircular; the compound eyes do not protrude and are relatively small for the head capsule (W/E 3.4–3.8), slightly angular-oval; the ocelli are small, oval, separated from the compound eyes by about 1.5 times their own least diameter; the postclypeus is strongly arched, 2.2 times as wide as long, its anterior margin slightly concave; the antennae are 15-segmented, segments II, IV and V nearly equal in length, II thinner, III longer. Mandibles: the apical tooth of the left mandible is equal to or slightly shorter than the first marginal tooth, the distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth being about one-third of the distance between the first and third marginal teeth (index 0.32–0.36), the second marginal tooth is absent, and the cutting edge between the first and third marginal teeth is entire; in the right mandible the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth are nearly equal, and the first marginal tooth bears a small accessory tooth proximally; the molar plate of the right mandible has a weak concavity at the base near the anterior margin, its posterior margin extended into a rounded ridge, the first transverse ridge forming a coarse tooth and the remaining 6–7 diminishing towards the base; the fontanelle is very narrow, slit-like, hardly forked anteriorly (more pronounced in the female), slightly paler to distinctly paler than the head colour.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic. The nasus is conical. The mandibles are reduced, with a small point. The head capsule is sharply constricted behind the antennal fossae, the posterior lobe usually only about a quarter wider than the anterior part. Antennae 12-segmented. Head capsule sepia-brown to pitch black, the nasus black with a reddish apex; the lateral contour of the head is raised and rounded behind the constriction and flatter before it; the nasus is equal to or shorter than the remainder of the head capsule measured from the posterior margin of the antennal fossae; the nasus cone angle is 10–20°; antennal segment II is short, IV and V longer; setae are confined to 4 at the tip of the nasus, a pair on the dorsum of the head, and a few short curved hairs on the dorsum. Specimen no. 25: head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.17–1.39 mm, head width 0.54–0.66 mm, hind tibia 0.92–1.10 mm.

/genus/rhinotermes/.note: The generic characters are Hill's quotation of Holmgren's definition, given verbatim; the alate, soldier and worker passages all come from that quotation. The Australian species are placed in the subgenus Schedorhinotermes, so most of the species-level material recorded in the paper does not belong to the nominal subgenus of the genus; only generic and subgeneric statements were used here, and species-level characters of the Australian species were not mixed in.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier occurs in two forms, major and minor, both with a forked labrum; the major soldier has very stout and strong mandibles, the left with two strong teeth and the right with one, the bases not finely serrate; the minor soldier has relatively longer, narrower and straighter mandibles with narrower and sharper teeth, or reduced mandibles; the labrum is relatively short and broad in the major soldier and in the minor soldier extends beyond the mandibles, being forked and grooved at the tip, either rather broad or extremely narrow; antennae 14–17 segments; pronotum small, far narrower than the head; styli present. In the alate of the subgenus Rhinotermes s. str. the clypeus is strong and beak-shaped and covers the base of the labrum, the head is relatively large, and in the minor soldier the labrum is forked and the mandibles are reduced.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head almost circular; clypeus more or less strongly arched, with a median longitudinal groove; fontanelle open and relatively wide, situated anteriorly; antennae 20–22 segments, segment 3 longer than segment 2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Occurring in two forms, major and minor, with a forked labrum. Major soldier: mandibles stout and very strong, the left with two strong teeth and the right with one, the mandibular bases without fine teeth; labrum relatively short and broad, forked and grooved at the tip. Minor soldier: mandibles relatively longer, narrower and straighter, with narrower and sharper teeth, or reduced; labrum extending beyond the mandibles, forked and grooved at the tip. Antennae 14–17 segments in both forms; pronotum small, far narrower than the head; styli present.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae 16–18 segments, segment 3 longer than segment 2; pronotum saddle-shaped.

/genus/rhynchotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, p. 55). In the original, Rhynchotermes is a subgenus of Armitermes (Untergattung), with no separate genus-level description: only three key characters (one each for the alate, soldier and worker) and one species, so each section is very short and does not go beyond what the key provides.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Established by Holmgren 1912 as a subgenus of Armitermes (Rhynchotermes n. subg.), at that time containing only the species nasutissimus (Mato Grosso, Paraguay, Bolivia). The differences from the other subgenera of the genus are given in the key: in the alate mandibular tooth 1 and tooth 2 are equal in size, the antennae have 14 segments and segment 3 is longer than the adjacent ones; in the soldier the mandibles are fairly robust and very strongly curved, with a quadrangular tooth in the middle, a very well-developed base bearing a sharp molar prominence, the 'nasus' (frontal tube) very long, and each fore coxa with a tooth-like projection; in the worker mandibular tooth 1 and tooth 2 are equal in length.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Mandibular tooth 1 and tooth 2 equal in size; antennae of 14 segments, segment 3 longer than the adjacent ones.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles fairly robust, very strongly curved, with a quadrangular tooth in the middle; the base very strongly developed, with a sharp molar prominence. The 'nasus' (frontal tube) very long. Each fore coxa with a tooth-like projection.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibular tooth 1 and tooth 2 equal in length. The original gives only this single key character for the worker of the subgenus, without further description.

/genus/roisinitermes/.note: At genus level only the alate and soldier sections are provided; the original does not treat the worker separately (the species has pseudergates and short-winged nymphs, and the nymphs only have species-level measurement tables), so no "Worker" or "Nymph" sections are set. No measurements are given at genus level; all measurements are species-level (alate Table 1, soldier Table 2).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The only genus in the Kalotermitidae with snapping mandibles: soldier mandibles slender and rod-like, the dentition extremely weak; the alate has no visible ocelli, also unique in the family. In Krishna's (1961) generic key the alate runs to couplet 2 (Epicalotermes) and the soldier to couplet 17 (Allotermes). The soldier mandibles are somewhat similar to the slender, nearly toothless mandibles of Allotermes (especially A. denticulatus), but in this genus the mandibles curve downwards in lateral view, which is unique among kalotermitids with forward-projecting mandibles; although the wing venation and dentition of the alate are very close to those of Epicalotermes, the soldier shares no major character with it.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and pronotum pale brownish orange, abdominal tergites paler, concolorous with the legs and labrum; postclypeus nearly transparent. Compound eyes medium-sized and prominent, oval, truncate near the antennal sockets, composed of about 85 ommatidia; ocelli neither pigmented nor with a cuticular projection, completely invisible. Antennae with more than 9 segments, segment formula 1>2=3=4<5 (species-level records 14–17 segments). Pronotum about 2 times as wide as its median length, lateral margins with several long setae and shorter setae. Forewing M and Cu stalked beyond the scale suture, the radial sector (Rs) with 5–6 anterior branches, the subcosta (Sc) closely appressed to the costa and difficult to distinguish; hindwing Rs and Cu stalked behind the suture. Tibial spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi without an arolium.
