Two pairs of horn-like processes at the front of the head: the upper pair, above and in front of the antennal sockets, arises from the lateral margin of the postclypeus and is termed the frontal horn; the lower pair, below and in front of the antennal sockets, is formed by prolongation of the genae and is termed the genal horn, its shape varying with the species. Frontal surface mostly concave; compound eyes generally visible, unpigmented. Antennae 11–15-segmented, clypeus slightly trapezoidal, labrum nearly triangular or ligulate. Mandibles short, the outer margin convex at the middle, the posterior part of the postmentum broad. Pronotum about as wide as the head capsule, its anterior margin deeply concave, mostly wavy or dentate. Legs short, tibial spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented, cerci 2-segmented.

/genus/cucurbitermes/.alate: Dealate head with long and short hairs interspersed with setae, the pronotum with rather many setae. Head nearly circular; fontanelle large and elongate-oval, not forked anteriorly, with a longitudinal line running from it to the posterior margin; postclypeus raised, with another longitudinal line at its centre; compound eyes large, elliptical and convex outwards, ocelli oval and slightly convex. Apical tooth of the left mandible as long as the first marginal tooth, the cutting edge between the two teeth nearly straight. Antennae 15-segmented. Anterior margin of the pronotum nearly straight, the posterior margin slightly concave at the middle. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/cucurbitermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Cucurbitermes section of the original book)
/genus/cucurbitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier monomorphic or dimorphic; head almost bare, the nasus with only a few hairs at its apex, constricted like a gourd at the base of the nasus and at the antennal sockets; nasus a slender tube; mandibles blunt and convex, without pointed tips; antennae 13–14-segmented; anterior half of the pronotum upright.
/genus/cucurbitermes/.distribution: Oriental region; a subtropical element, recorded from southern and south-eastern China.
/genus/cucurbitermes/.soldier: Soldier monomorphic or dimorphic. Head almost bare, with only a few hairs at the apex of the nasus, the thoracic tergites hairless. Excluding the nasus, the head is about as long as wide, or slightly wider than long; constricted like a gourd at the base of the nasus and at the antennal sockets, strongly convex behind the antennal sockets, the sides rounded, the posterior margin rather flat; nasus slender and tubular. Mandibles blunt and convex, without pointed tips. Antennae 13–14-segmented. The anterior half of the pronotum stands upright, at about a right angle to the posterior half. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.

/genus/dicuspiditermes/.alate: Alate with a broad oval head capsule, slightly narrowed anteriorly, densely covered with long and short hairs. Fontanelle generally slender, slit-like; compound eyes elliptical; ocelli oval and separate from the compound eyes. Postclypeus raised. Apical tooth of the left mandible short, slightly larger than or almost equal to the first marginal tooth, which in turn is larger than the second; the posterior margin of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible long. Antennae 14–15-segmented.
/genus/dicuspiditermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Dicuspiditermes section of the original book)
/genus/dicuspiditermes/.diagnosis: Soldier with a rectangular head, the anterior part raised; an anterolateral process below each antennal socket; mandibles asymmetrical, the left twisted into a hook, the right straight as a blade; lateral corners of the labrum projecting forwards like needles; antennae 14-segmented; pronotum saddle-shaped.
/genus/dicuspiditermes/.distribution: Oriental region; distributed in tropical and subtropical areas, recorded from southern China.
/genus/dicuspiditermes/.soldier: Soldier with a rectangular head capsule, the anterior part raised, with an anterolateral horn-like process on each side below the antennal sockets. Mandibles asymmetrical: the left twisted, its apex curved inwards into a hook; the right straighter, blade-like. Anterior margin of the labrum deeply concave, the lateral corners slender as needles and projecting far forwards. Antennae 14-segmented. Pronotum saddle-shaped, its width far less than the head width.

/genus/euhamitermes/.biology: Euhamitermes live underground beside grass roots and feed on decaying plant material; colonies are small and mostly lack soldiers, so identification is quite difficult. The species of this genus are rather secretive in their activity, and specimens often have to be obtained by digging.
/genus/euhamitermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Euhamitermes section of the original book)
/genus/euhamitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head capsule between rectangular and square; mandibles stout and short, strongly curved like hooks, with a small tooth at the middle of the inner margin; pronotum strongly saddle-shaped; spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented; soldiers are not easily collected.
/genus/euhamitermes/.distribution: Oriental region; 24 species are known worldwide, 13 in China, with Yunnan accounting for about half of the national total.
/genus/euhamitermes/.soldier: Soldier head capsule intermediate between rectangular and square. Mandibles stout and short, strongly curved like hooks, with a small tooth at the middle of the inner margin. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped. Spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented. Because colonies are small and often lack soldiers, specimens are not easily obtained.

/genus/globitermes/.alate: Alate rather small; head capsule thick and slightly convex; compound eyes very small; fontanelle distinct. Postclypeus wider than the frons, its surface rather flat, less than half as long as wide; labrum wider than long; antennae 15–16-segmented. Pronotum more than half as long as wide. Forewing scale slightly longer than the hindwing scale, the wing surface densely covered with fine punctures; the media of the forewing arises independently at the humeral suture, that of the hindwing branches from the radial sector close to the cubitus. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2.
/genus/globitermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Globitermes section of the original book)
/genus/globitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier with a short, thick, nearly circular head capsule; mandibles slender with hooked apices, each mandible with a sharp tooth at the middle of the inner margin; labrum bluntly rounded anteriorly; antennae at most 15-segmented; alate with very small compound eyes, the media of the forewing arising independently at the humeral suture.
/genus/globitermes/.distribution: Oriental region; a component of tropical and subtropical forests, recorded from southern China.
/genus/globitermes/.soldier: Soldier with a short, thick head capsule, nearly circular in outline, yellow in colour. Mandibles slender, the anterior portion curved into a hook, each mandible with a sharp marginal tooth at the middle of the inner margin. Labrum oval, bluntly rounded without a point at the apex. Antennae with no more than 15 segments. Postmentum distinctly raised upwards at the middle. Pronotum narrower than the head, slightly convex anteriorly and at the middle.

/genus/glyptotermes/.alate: The alate largely resembles that of Kalotermes, differing in that the media of the wing is straight and closely appressed to the radial sector, and neither media nor radius branches. Antennae 12–15-segmented, spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented; the structure of the legs and wings is similar to that of Kalotermes.
/genus/glyptotermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Glyptotermes section of the original book)
/genus/glyptotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier with an elongate head capsule, the vertex often raised above the rest and forming twin peaks; mandibles short and stout, much shorter relative to head length than in Neotermes; antennae short, mostly 10–12-segmented; labrum square; tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/glyptotermes/.distribution: Recorded from the Oriental, Australian, Neotropical and Afrotropical regions.
/genus/glyptotermes/.soldier: Soldier with an elongate head capsule, the vertex usually higher than the rest of the head, forming twin peaks. Frontal surface either sloping or steep; in some species the frontal wrinkles are coarse and deep, in others smooth or with punctate sculpture. Antennae short, mostly 10–12-segmented. Mandibles short and stout, much shorter relative to head length than in Neotermes, with several distinct marginal teeth, the basal ridge of the mandible prominent or flat. Pronotum flattened and broad. Labrum mostly square. Femora not thickened. Spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented.

/genus/hodotermopsis/.biology: Hodotermopsis mainly attacks primary and secondary forest, boring into living standing trees and also feeding on stumps, and in severe cases invading dwellings and historic buildings. It mostly inhabits moist forest and feeds on timber containing moisture, hence the name dampwood termite.
/genus/hodotermopsis/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Hodotermopsis section of the original book)
/genus/hodotermopsis/.diagnosis: Soldier with a broad, flat, nearly circular head capsule, the posterior and lateral margins arcuate; antennae up to 24-segmented; compound eyes distinct; mandibles stout and strongly curved, the left with four marginal teeth, the right with three; pronotum flat, slightly narrower than the head.
/genus/hodotermopsis/.soldier: Soldier with a broad, flat head, nearly circular in outline, the posterior and lateral margins arcuate. Antennae with many segments, up to 24; compound eyes clearly visible. Mandibles strong, strongly curved, the tooth row well developed, the left mandible with four marginal teeth, the right with three. Pronotum flat, slightly narrower than the head capsule, its anterior margin slightly concave. The hind tibia bears two lateral spines in addition to the four apical spurs, while the fore and mid tibiae lack lateral spines. Cerci 4–6-segmented.

/genus/hospitalitermes/.alate: Alate dark in both body and wings. Head broadly oval; postclypeus less than half as long as wide; frons triangularly depressed behind the postclypeus. Forewing and hindwing scales similar in size; radius absent; media closely appressed to the cubitus. Antennae 15-segmented, the third segment about twice as long as the second.
/genus/hospitalitermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Hospitalitermes section of the original book)
/genus/hospitalitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier dark in colour; nasus slender, deeply concave where it meets the head; mandibles reduced while the pointed tips are very long; antennae 14-segmented with the third segment not shorter than the fourth; anterior part of the pronotum raised; legs very long; alate entirely dark.
/genus/hospitalitermes/.distribution: Oriental region; a group of tropical rainforest and monsoon forest, recorded from southern China.
/genus/hospitalitermes/.soldier: Soldier mostly dark in colour. Head with a rather slender nasus, markedly concave where the nasus meets the head capsule. Mandibles much reduced, only a very small mandibular base remaining, but the pointed tips very long, their surface smooth and toothless. Antennae 14-segmented, the third segment equal to or slightly longer than the fourth. Anterior part of the pronotum raised. Legs very long, their segments slender.

/genus/hypotermes/.alate: Alate head reddish brown; anteclypeus white, postclypeus pale yellowish brown, antennae brown; the pronotum slightly darker in colour than the head and bearing a T-shaped mark, each of the two anterior lateral corners with a ring-shaped spot resembling an ocellus. Head and postclypeus densely covered with short hairs, interspersed with sparse long hairs. Head outline semicircular; fontanelle small and round; compound eyes not very regularly rounded, protruding slightly outwards; ocelli broadly oval. Postclypeus about half as long as wide, the median longitudinal line clear; labrum arcuate; anteclypeus trapezoidal; antennae with nineteen segments. Pronotum narrower than the head, half-moon shaped in outline; its anterior margin roughly straight, the median notch very shallow, and the posterior margin slightly concave in the middle.
/genus/hypotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Hypotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/hypotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head oval, slightly narrowed anteriorly, body colour pale yellowish brown; labrum arcuate, slightly longer than wide; the middle of the left mandible with three marginal teeth, the right mandible with serrated small teeth before the base; antennae with fifteen to sixteen segments.
/genus/hypotermes/.distribution: Oriental Region; in China the species occur in western and southern Yunnan.
/genus/hypotermes/.soldier: Soldier head pale yellowish brown to brown, paler anteriorly; pronotum yellow, antennae brown, labrum pale brown, mandibles pale reddish brown. Head surface sparsely haired; the anterior half of the labrum with several long hairs around its margin, the anterior margin of the postmentum also with long hairs, long hairs scattered over the pronotum. Head oval, slightly narrowed anteriorly. Labrum arcuate, slightly longer than wide. Mandibles slender and incurved, the middle of the left mandible with three marginal teeth, the right mandible with serrated small teeth before the base. Postmentum arcuate, the two sides slightly straight. Antennae with fifteen to sixteen segments, occasionally seventeen. Anterior and posterior margins of the pronotum both slightly concave in the middle.

/genus/incisitermes/.alate: Alate body colour mostly pale brown, some species dark brown. Compound eyes round and large, ocelli close against the compound eyes, the two almost touching. Antennae with thirteen to twenty segments. Left and right mandibles each with two marginal teeth. Pronotum usually slightly wider than the head, or as wide as the head. Wing membrane transparent, without nodular structures, tibial spur formula 3:3:3, most species with an arolium between the claws.
/genus/incisitermes/.biology: Incisitermes colonies are small and simply built, tolerate drought and are readily spread by human transport, so they deserve attention in quarantine. Incisitermes minor was introduced into China in the late 1940s and formerly damaged large buildings in Nanjing, Shanghai, Ningbo and elsewhere; after control the Nanjing population has not been seen for many years.
/genus/incisitermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Incisitermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/incisitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head capsule flattened, rectangular, the two sides parallel, the frontal slope very small; antennae with ten to seventeen segments, the third longest and club-shaped; pronotum as wide as or slightly wider than the head, its anterior margin deeply concave, tibial spur formula 3:3:3.
/genus/incisitermes/.distribution: Nearctic, Neotropical and Oriental Regions; in China only Incisitermes minor is known, introduced from abroad.
/genus/incisitermes/.soldier: Soldier head flattened, rectangular, the two lateral margins parallel to each other, the frontal surface sloping very gently. Mandibles stout. Antennae with ten to seventeen segments, the third longest, club-shaped and heavily sclerotised. Pronotum as wide as or slightly wider than the head capsule, its anterior margin deeply concave. Femora stout, tibial spur formula 3:3:3.

/genus/indotermes/.alate: Alate head nearly circular, ocelli and compound eyes both small, postclypeus markedly raised, its length equal to or slightly less than half its width, the posterior margin arcuately curved, fontanelle distinct and situated posteriorly, antennae with fifteen segments. Wing membrane brown, the media of the forewing arising from the radial sector and closely adjacent to the cubitus. Anterior margin of the pronotum slightly concave in the middle, the posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum each with a narrow, pointed triangular notch. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi three-segmented.
/genus/indotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Indotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/indotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head capsule stout and broadly cylindrical, the lateral margins nearly parallel, each mandible with one marginal tooth, postmentum broad, short and flat; alate with small ocelli and compound eyes, fontanelle posterior, the media of the forewing arising from the radial sector, tarsi with only three tarsomeres.
/genus/indotermes/.distribution: Oriental Region; a tropical and subtropical element, recorded in southern China.
/genus/indotermes/.soldier: Soldier head capsule broadly cylindrical, very stout, the lateral margins nearly parallel, broadly rounded posteriorly. Body colour mainly yellowish brown, mandibles of the same colour but reddish brown to almost black apically, labrum and antennae pale. Head densely covered with fine hairs, thorax and abdomen with intermingled long and short hairs. Mandibles strong, each with one marginal tooth; labrum short and small, its margin transparent; antennae with fourteen segments; postmentum flat, broad and short. Pronotum extremely narrow and short, the anterior lobe semicircular and erect, less than half the width of the head. Tarsi three-segmented.

/genus/kalotermes/.alate: Alate head slightly convex, the lateral margins parallel, the posterior margin broadly arcuate, outline nearly quadrilateral. Postclypeus extremely short, not divided into two lobes. The posterior margin of the first marginal tooth of the left mandible is fused with the second marginal tooth and longer than the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth. Antennae with sixteen to nineteen segments, ocelli slightly separated from the compound eyes. Pronotum broad and flat, the notch of the anterior margin broadly arcuate, the two sides slightly parallel and symmetrical, the posterior margin broad, the median notch shallow and wide. The anterior margin of the forewing scale projecting, longer than or equal to the pronotum and much larger than the hindwing scale. Rs divided into several branches. The media of the forewing not sclerotised, arising within the wing scale of Cu and running between Rs and Cu. Legs very short, tibial spur formula 3:3:3, with an arolium, cerci indistinct.
/genus/kalotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Kalotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/kalotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head large, rectangular, the two sides rather flat; mandibles stout, longer than half the head length, the inner margin with many teeth of unequal size; antennae with thirteen to eighteen segments, the third swollen; tibial spur formula 3:3:3.
/genus/kalotermes/.distribution: Oriental Region; species of this genus are recorded from every province and autonomous region of southern China.
/genus/kalotermes/.soldier: Soldier head large, rectangular, the two sides rather flat, the dorsal margin straight in lateral view. Frons slightly projecting, sloping towards the clypeus. Mandibles stout and somewhat elongate, longer than half the head length, the inner margin bearing many teeth of unequal size. Antennae with thirteen to eighteen segments, the third distinctly enlarged. Pale eye spots visible behind the antennal sockets. Postmentum somewhat elongate, the waist at the middle or slightly behind it, the widest part with the two sides nearly parallel in the anterior two-thirds, slightly concave in the middle. Pronotum broad and flat, the median notch of the anterior margin wide and shallow, the two sides nearly parallel, the middle of the posterior margin slightly concave. Femora thick, legs short, with three tibial spurs, formula 3:3:3.

/genus/macrotermes/.alate: Alate head broadly oval, fontanelle distinct and slightly raised, ocelli fairly large. Postclypeus convex, about half as long as wide, the posterior margin arcuate and the anterior margin straight. Antennae with nineteen segments, the third longer than the second. The posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum form shallow arcuate incisions. Radius projecting slightly beyond the wing scale; the media of the forewing arises independently at the humeral suture, the media of the hindwing mostly from the base of the radial sector. The lateral walls of the queen's abdomen without dense coloured dots.
/genus/macrotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Macrotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/macrotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier usually of two sizes, major and minor, or of three, major, medium and minor; the two sides of the head parallel or narrowed anteriorly, frons flat, fontanelle punctiform; mandibles curved like sickles, the base of the left mandible with several notches and a distinct basal tooth; antennae with seventeen segments.
/genus/macrotermes/.distribution: Oriental and Afrotropical Regions; recorded from every province and autonomous region of southern China.
/genus/macrotermes/.soldier: Soldier usually of two sizes, major and minor, some species also with a medium size, three in all. The two sides of the head parallel, or narrowed anteriorly. Frons flat, fontanelle punctiform. Labrum widest at the middle, with a small transparent patch at the apex. Mandibles curved like sickles; the base of the left mandible with several notches and one distinct basal tooth, no other teeth besides the basal one; the right mandible likewise toothed only at the base. Antennae with seventeen segments, the third often longer than the second. Pronotum saddle-shaped, both its anterior and posterior margins notched.

/genus/microcerotermes/.alate: Alate head capsule oval, the lateral margins straight; compound eyes not large, protruding outwards. Ocelli small, slightly separated from the compound eyes. The frontal gland opening is often difficult to see. Postclypeus slightly raised, lower than the frons, its anterior margin straight. Antennae with thirteen to fourteen segments. Pronotum small, much narrower than the head capsule; the posterior part of the mesonotum wider than the metanotum. Wing membrane pale brown to dark brown, densely covered with short hairs; radius absent or vestigial; media close to the cubitus. Male with styli. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2.
/genus/microcerotermes/.biology: This genus damages many kinds of crops, forest trees and buildings. In the Arabian Peninsula and elsewhere a Middle Eastern Microcerotermes severely damages timber-framed buildings as well as date palms, cotton and citrus, while in tropical Africa a Microcerotermes with dark tibiae damages cotton and maize. Species of this genus have been intercepted many times in quarantine on timber imported into China.
/genus/microcerotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Microcerotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/microcerotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head capsule rectangular and thick; frontal pore indistinct; mandibles long and sickle-shaped, the outer margin of the mandibular base mostly concave, the inner margin serrated; antennae with twelve to thirteen segments; pronotum saddle-shaped, much narrower than the head.
/genus/microcerotermes/.distribution: Oriental Region, Australasia, Africa and the Americas; five species are at present known from China, mostly in Yunnan and Hainan, closely related to species of the Indochinese Peninsula.
/genus/microcerotermes/.soldier: Soldier head capsule rectangular, fairly thick. Frontal pore indistinct. The posterior margin of the postclypeus raised upwards. Labrum large, its apex rounded or truncate. Mandibles long, sickle-shaped to sabre-shaped, the outer margin of the base mostly concave inwards, the inner margin serrated. Antennae with twelve to thirteen segments. Pronotum saddle-shaped, much narrower than the head capsule. Styli poorly developed.

/genus/microtermes/.alate: Alate head brown with a faint smoky tinge, postclypeus yellow, labrum pale brown with a milky white apex, antennae yellowish brown. Head surface haired, the labrum with several long hairs near the apex, the rest short, the pronotum densely covered with short hairs. Head nearly circular, fontanelle small and round, compound eyes raised like round domes, ocelli rather large, labrum arched and slightly wider than long, the first marginal tooth of the mandible close to the tooth apex, antennae with fifteen segments. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head, the middle of both the anterior and the posterior margins slightly concave.
/genus/microtermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Microtermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/microtermes/.diagnosis: Soldier body colour pale, head elongate oval, narrow anteriorly and broad posteriorly, the vertex raised like a dome in lateral view, antennae with fourteen segments, the middle of both the anterior and the posterior margins of the pronotum concave; alate with fifteen antennal segments, ocelli rather large, compound eyes round and raised.
/genus/microtermes/.distribution: Oriental and Afrotropical Regions; a tropical and subtropical group, with several species in southern China.
/genus/microtermes/.soldier: Soldier head capsule and labrum pale yellow, mandibles reddish brown, antennae milky white, pronotum, abdomen and legs nearly milky white. Head densely covered with fine short hairs, the labrum with both apical hairs and long and short hairs. Head elongate oval, narrowed anteriorly and widened posteriorly, the middle of the vertex raised like a dome in lateral view. Labrum mostly lanceolate; the middle of the left mandible slightly arched, with small teeth before the basal tooth; the right mandible slightly more slender than the left; postmentum widest at the middle; antennae with fourteen segments. The middle of both the anterior and the posterior margins of the pronotum concave.

/genus/nasutitermes/.alate: Alate entirely dark. Head broadly oval, postclypeus paler in colour, its width several times its length, fontanelle small, mostly elongate and forked. Antennal segments not much elongated. The incisions of the posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum are both fairly wide. Forewing scale and hindwing scale similar in size, radius absent, media very close to the cubitus.
/genus/nasutitermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Nasutitermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/nasutitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head circular or elongate oval, the nasus projecting from the front of the frons as a tube or a cone, the middle of the head not constricted, no constriction behind the antennal sockets, mandibles minute and labrum very short, soldiers generally monomorphic; alate entirely dark.
/genus/nasutitermes/.distribution: Neotropical, Nearctic, Afrotropical, Oriental and Australian Regions; rather many species in southern China.
/genus/nasutitermes/.soldier: Soldier head capsule circular or elongate oval, the nasus projecting from the front of the frons, either tubular or conical, narrow anteriorly and broad posteriorly, the middle of the head not constricted. The junction of the vertex and the nasus straight, or slightly concave. No constriction behind the antennal sockets. Mandibles minute, their anterior lateral corners obtusely rounded, or produced into sharp points. Antennal segments not very long. Labrum very short. Soldiers of this genus generally of a single size.

/genus/neotermes/.alate: Alate head outline somewhat square, the posterior lateral corners broadly rounded, the two sides and the middle of the posterior margin rather straight. The inner margin of each mandible with two marginal teeth, the apical tooth slightly longer than the first marginal tooth, the posterior margin of the first marginal tooth of the left mandible fused with the second marginal tooth and longer than the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth. Labrum short, broad and tongue-shaped. Antennae with sixteen to nineteen segments, the third not larger than the second or the fourth. Compound eyes fairly large, projecting outwards below the lower margin of the head, the pair of ocelli on their inner side touching the compound eyes. Postmentum narrow and long. Pronotum transversely rectangular, short and broad, wider than the head, the median notch of the anterior margin broadly arcuate, the middle of the posterior margin slightly concave. Forewing scale large, its anterior margin projecting and covering the hindwing scale, media sclerotised. Legs slender, spur formula 3:3:3, an arolium between the claws, cerci with two segments.
/genus/neotermes/.biology: Neotermes species are wood-dwelling termites, usually living in damp wood that contains some moisture and in living tree trunks, hence they are also called dampwood termites. Besides damaging trees, they can also attack timber-framed houses and economic forest trees; in the swarming season a pair of reproductives may enter wood, tree stumps or structural timber to found a new colony and gradually spread the damage.
/genus/neotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Neotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/neotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head rectangular, the frontal region raised and gradually sloping towards the clypeus; the inner margin of the left mandible with four to five marginal teeth, the right with two; antennae with twelve to sixteen segments, the third not especially swollen; cerci with two segments.
/genus/neotermes/.distribution: Oriental Region, also found in the Americas and elsewhere; recorded from every province and autonomous region of southern China.
/genus/neotermes/.soldier: Soldier fairly large, head rectangular, the dorsal and ventral surfaces rather flat. Frontal region raised, gradually sloping towards the clypeus. Mandibles stout and rather long, the inner margin of the left with four to five marginal teeth, the right with two. Labrum short and broad, its anterior margin broadly arcuate and the sides rounded, tongue-shaped. Antennae with twelve to sixteen segments, the third not especially swollen, slightly longer or slightly shorter than the second. Pale eye spots behind the antennal sockets. Postmentum with the sides of the widest part slightly concave or notched at the middle, the outline parallel or slightly narrowed posteriorly, the waist central. The median notch of the anterior margin of the pronotum broadly arcuate and shallow, the middle of the posterior margin slightly concave or nearly straight. Femora not swollen, tibial spur formula 3:3:3.

/genus/odontotermes/.alate: Alate head broadly oval or nearly circular, fontanelle distinct. Postclypeus raised, slightly paler in colour than the vertex, very short, about half as long as wide. Antennae with nineteen segments, the third often shorter than the second. Pronotum often with a pale cruciform marking and spots on the anterior sides, the posterior part of the lateral margins contracted. The posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum arcuately concave. Wings transparent to dark brown, radius very short, the media of the forewing arising from the base of the cubitus, the media of the hindwing arising from the radius. The lateral walls of the queen's abdomen covered with small brown dots.
/genus/odontotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Odontotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/odontotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head oval, longer than wide, the anterior end often narrow; frons flat, fontanelle indistinct; labrum without a transparent tip, long hairs on the two lateral margins; the left mandible with one large pointed tooth; antennae with fifteen to eighteen segments.
/genus/odontotermes/.distribution: Oriental Region; distributed throughout the provinces and autonomous regions of southern China, more numerous in South China and Southwest China.
/genus/odontotermes/.soldier: Soldier head oval, longer than wide, the anterior end often narrowed. Frons flat, fontanelle not very distinct. Labrum without a transparent tip, long hairs on the two lateral margins. Mandibles curved, sabre-shaped, the left mandible with one large pointed tooth. Antennae with fifteen to eighteen segments. Postmentum rectangular, very wide at the middle. Pronotum narrower than the head, saddle-shaped.

/genus/parrhinotermes/.biology: Parrhinotermes is a small genus of Isoptera, at present comprising seven species together with the Chinese ones. Its species live in evergreen broad-leaved forest, mostly in tropical and marginally tropical areas; affected by the uplift of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, the Chinese species reach as far north as the southern Hengduan Mountains.
/genus/parrhinotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Parrhinotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/parrhinotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head oval and flattened, fontanelle small, frontal gland well developed, labrum elongated and club-shaped; mandibles long and sabre-like, the base of the inner margin densely set with eighteen to twenty-one small serrations; antennae with thirteen segments, pronotum narrower than the head.
/genus/parrhinotermes/.distribution: Oriental Region; in China recorded from the Medog area of Tibet, abroad from Assam in India and elsewhere.
/genus/parrhinotermes/.soldier: Soldier head oval, rather flat, fontanelle pore small, frontal gland well developed. Labrum elongated, club-shaped. Mandibles long, sabre-shaped, the base of the inner margin densely set with eighteen to twenty-one small serrations. Postmentum small and flat. Antennae with thirteen segments. Pronotum flat, narrower than the head capsule.

/genus/periaciculitermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account of Periaciculitermes in the original book, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/periaciculitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head oval, narrow anteriorly and broad posteriorly, the dorsum with short hairs, widest at about one third of the head from the posterior margin, posterior margin slightly arcuate with the middle a little flattened; nasus straight, slender and elongate, slightly raised behind its base; mandibles bluntly convex, without sharp teeth; antennae 12-segmented.
/genus/periaciculitermes/.distribution: Oriental region; a tropical and subtropical element, recorded from southern China.
/genus/periaciculitermes/.soldier: Soldier head with short hairs mixed with a few long setae. Head oval, anteriorly narrow and posteriorly broad, widest at about one third from the posterior margin of the head, the posterior margin slightly arcuate and rounded but flatter at the middle; in lateral view the junction between the posterior margin of the nasus base and the head capsule is slightly raised. Nasus straight, tubular and slender. Mandibles bluntly convex, without sharp teeth. Antennae 12-segmented. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/periaciculitermes/.worker: The apical tooth of the worker left mandible is distinctly larger than the first marginal tooth; the second marginal tooth is reduced and fused with the posterior cutting edge of the first marginal tooth; the third marginal tooth is very small, its anterior cutting edge meeting the posterior cutting edge of the first marginal tooth at an acute angle. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.

/genus/pericapritermes/.alate: Alate head broadly oval, slightly narrowed anteriorly; postclypeus slightly convex, less than half as long as wide, with or without a median suture. Antennae 14–15-segmented; fontanelle oval. The inner margin of the apical tooth of the left mandible is as long as or slightly longer than the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth, while its apical distance is shorter than the distance between the first and third marginal teeth; the second marginal tooth of the right mandible is well developed, its posterior curved margin arcuate; the apical distance between the second and first marginal teeth is shorter than that between the first marginal tooth and the apical tooth. The anterior margin of the pronotum is slightly concave at the middle.
/genus/pericapritermes/.biology: The mandibles of these termites are particularly well developed and strongly twisted, enabling the insects to spring by means of them while emitting a clicking sound. Nests are mostly built in the soil and consist of several chambers and passages; they feed on plant rootlets and decaying parts, and can also bore into the surface of living trees and into sugar cane. One species of the genus is recorded as feeding on fungal spores and water in the soil.
/genus/pericapritermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account of Pericapritermes in the original book, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/pericapritermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head rectangular with a rather flat dorsal margin, the frons sloping; the apex of the left mandible blunt and not hooked, the inner cutting edge slightly concave at the middle; labrum about as long as wide; antennae 13–16-segmented, tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/pericapritermes/.distribution: Oriental region; mainly tropical and subtropical, common in the provinces of south-western and south-eastern coastal China.
/genus/pericapritermes/.soldier: Soldier head rectangular, the lateral margins nearly parallel, the dorsal margin fairly straight. Frons sloping or slightly steep, fontanelle dot-like. The cephalic suture is fairly distinct, extending forwards to before the middle. Mandibles strongly asymmetrical: the apex of the left mandible is blunt or curved inwards, its tip slightly flattened and not hooked, the inner cutting edge slightly concave at the middle; the right mandible is straighter, or its anterior part slightly curved outwards. Labrum about as long as wide, the anterior margin straight, the lateral corners pointed and shortly projecting; postclypeus very narrow. Antennae 13–16-segmented. Pronotum saddle-shaped, narrower than the head. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.

/genus/pilotermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account of Pilotermes in the original book, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/pilotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier dimorphic: the head of the major soldier is nearly circular, deeply emarginate at the middle of the posterior margin, the nasus shorter than the head width; the head of the minor soldier is elongate pyriform, the nasus longer than the head width; the mandibles in both lack sharp teeth, the sides of the middle of the postmentum are constricted waist-like, antennae 12–13-segmented.
/genus/pilotermes/.distribution: Oriental region; recorded from Jiangxi and other parts of China, an element of subtropical forests.
/genus/pilotermes/.soldier: Soldier in two forms, major and minor. In the major soldier the head and nasus are densely covered with fine short hairs, while the dorsum of the pronotum is bare. Head nearly circular, slightly broader than long, deeply emarginate at the middle of the posterior margin, not constricted below the posterior side of the antennal sockets; nasus shorter than the head width, not constricted at the base; antennae 13-segmented; mandibles without sharp teeth; the sides of the middle of the postmentum narrowed waist-like. Pronotum broader than long, its anterior margin slightly concave at the middle, the posterior margin not concave. In the minor soldier the head is elongate pyriform, longer than broad, the middle of the posterior margin slightly concave, the nasus longer than the head width, slightly raised at the base like a small mound, antennae 12-segmented, the sharp teeth of the mandibles absent or very inconspicuous. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2 in both forms, tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/pilotermes/.worker: Worker with a Y-shaped suture on the dorsum of the head, antennae 13–14-segmented. The posterior margins of the apical teeth of both the left and right mandibles are longer than the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth; in the left mandible the anterior and posterior margins of the third marginal tooth are almost equal in length, and the first and second marginal teeth are fused; in the right mandible the apical distance between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth is shorter than that between the first and second marginal teeth. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.

/genus/prorhinotermes/.alate: Alate head capsule slightly longer than broad, oval; the frontal gland pore is distinct, and there is also a shallow groove in front of it. Postclypeus convex, much broader than long, with or without a median suture. Antennae 19–22-segmented. Pronotum broader than the head capsule or slightly narrower. Wing membrane sparsely hairy, the venation strongly reticulate, the media absent or arising from the cubitus, tibial spur formula 3:2:2.
/genus/prorhinotermes/.biology: Prorhinotermes attacks a variety of living trees and also feeds on dead and decaying parts. Prorhinotermes simplex is distributed over the Caribbean islands and has spread to the southern tip of the Florida peninsula in the United States, where it is regarded as a wood-destroying pest of buildings that cannot be ignored. The genus has long been considered an island-dwelling group, and its colonies are mostly built as honeycomb-like nests at the sites of attack.
/genus/prorhinotermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account of Prorhinotermes in the original book, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/prorhinotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head capsule oval or nearly trapezoidal, narrower in its anterior part; frontal gland pore obvious, with a shallow groove about one third of the head length in front of it; mandibles sabre-like, curved at the apex; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, antennae 16–19-segmented.
/genus/prorhinotermes/.distribution: Oriental region, Oceania, the Americas and Africa; four species known from China, recorded from Yunnan, Hainan, Taiwan and the Xisha Islands.
/genus/prorhinotermes/.soldier: Soldier head capsule oval or nearly trapezoidal, relatively narrow in its anterior part. Frontal gland pore distinct, with a shallow groove in front of it about one third of the length of the head capsule. Compound eyes distinct or already reduced. Antennae 16–19-segmented. Mandibles sabre-like, curved at the apex, the inner margin smooth, or with traces of fine teeth at the base. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

/genus/pseudocapritermes/.alate: Alate head capsule broadly oval. The distance between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth of the right mandible is slightly greater than the distance between the first and second marginal teeth. In the left mandible the posterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth together are long, forming almost a straight line. Postclypeus convex, without a distinct median suture. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2.
/genus/pseudocapritermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account of Pseudocapritermes in the original book, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/pseudocapritermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head rectangular, the left mandible twisted, its apex narrow and curved inwards into a hook, the right mandible straight as a sword, the two mandibles very different; labrum longer than wide, the anteromedian notch shallow and flat; antennae 14-segmented; pronotum much narrower than the head capsule, saddle-shaped.
/genus/pseudocapritermes/.distribution: Oriental region; 12 species are known in the genus, which is the only genus of the twisted-jaw termite group confined to the Oriental region, and seven species are recorded from China.
/genus/pseudocapritermes/.soldier: Soldier head capsule rectangular, the lateral margins slightly parallel, the frons not convex or slightly raised. Mandibles asymmetrical: the left mandible is twisted, narrowed at the apex and curved inwards into a hook; the right mandible is straighter, sword-like, its tip mostly slightly inclined inwards, occasionally projecting forwards or curved outwards. The two mandibles are very different. Labrum usually longer than wide, the anteromedian notch shallow and gentle. Antennae 14-segmented. Pronotum narrower than the head, saddle-shaped. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

/genus/reticulitermes/.alate: Alate body colour mostly dark, a few pale, the colour of the head, pronotum and legs varying with the group. Head nearly circular, fontanelle small and dot-like. Ocelli distinct; the degree of projection of the postclypeus varies with the group. Antennae 16–19-segmented, the second marginal tooth of the left mandible generally about as long as the first. Forewing scale slightly overlapping the hindwing scale, wings dark in colour, sparsely hairy or with needle-like hairs, the wing surface without spots, the cross-veins numerous and united into a distinct network; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented. Cerci 2-segmented; the stylus of the male 1-segmented, absent in the female.
/genus/reticulitermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account of Reticulitermes in the original book, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/reticulitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head rectangular, the lateral margins parallel or nearly so; fontanelle small and dot-like; labrum ligulate, its tip semicircular and bearing a pair of long apical setae; mandibles slender to stout, sabre-like or nearly hooked; tibial spur formula 3:2:2.
/genus/reticulitermes/.soldier: Soldier head rectangular, the lateral margins parallel or nearly parallel, the posterior margin broadly rounded or slightly straight. Frons from flat to strongly convex, flat or grooved between the frontal peaks. Fontanelle small, dot-like, rarely projecting. Labrum ligulate, its tip semicircular, bearing a pair of long apical setae; besides the pair of long apical setae, the subapical setae are either fine and small or slightly long, while the length of the lateral apical setae varies with the species and they are sometimes absent. Mandibles from slender to stout, sabre-like or curved and nearly hooked. Antennae 14–19-segmented. Legs slender and long, tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented; pronotum flat. The waist region of the postmentum is narrow and long. Stylus 1-segmented, cerci 2-segmented.

/genus/schedorhinotermes/.alate: Alate head capsule nearly circular, its fontanelle situated slightly in front of the midline of the vertex. Left mandible with three marginal teeth, the second distinctly shorter than the first and the third; right mandible with two marginal teeth, with an additional submarginal tooth in front of the first. Labrum broadly rounded, postclypeus convex with its apex projecting forwards. Antennae 20–22-segmented, the third segment longer than the second. The anterior margin of the pronotum projects slightly at the middle, the anterior part of the lateral margins is broad and the posterior part gradually narrows, so that together with the posterior margin they enclose a semicircle. Wings short and broad, the forewing scale larger, its media arising independently from the outer side of the basal suture, whereas the media of the hindwing arises from the radial sector and runs close to the cubitus, the cross-veins between them uniting into a network.
/genus/schedorhinotermes/.biology: Schedorhinotermes mainly damages living trees and fallen dead logs, and also attacks hard upright wooden utility poles as well as wooden members near the ground in buildings. Nests are generally built inside trees or in hollows in the middle of the trunk.
/genus/schedorhinotermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account of Schedorhinotermes in the original book, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/schedorhinotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier dimorphic: the head of the major soldier is short and broad, nearly square, that of the minor soldier slightly narrow and long; fontanelle circular, its opening situated between the antennal sockets, the longitudinal groove in front of the pore reaching the tip of the labrum; antennae of the major soldier 16–17-segmented, of the minor 13–16-segmented. In an individual Australian species (S. seclusus) the soldier is trimorphic.
/genus/schedorhinotermes/.distribution: Oriental region; six species known from China, mostly distributed in the Xishuangbanna and Simao areas of Yunnan, also recorded from Guangxi.
/genus/schedorhinotermes/.soldier: Soldier in two forms, major and minor. The major soldier has a short, broad, nearly square head; the fontanelle pore is circular, its opening between the antennal sockets, and the longitudinal groove in front of the pore reaches the tip of the labrum. Mandibles strong, either thick or flattened and broad, the anterior part curved inwards, with two large teeth on the inner margin of the left mandible and two teeth on the inner margin of the right mandible. Labrum rather short and broad, the sides of its middle slightly convex outwards so that it appears hexagonal, the anterior margin slightly concave at the middle, the tip with a transparent area, the anterior margin bearing a row of brush-like short hairs; antennae 16–17-segmented. The minor soldier has a slightly narrow and long head; the mandibles are slender and straighter, only slightly curved at the apex, with two marginal teeth on the inner margin of the left mandible and one on the right; the labrum is narrower and longer, its sides constricted waist-like at the middle, the transparent area at the tip slightly concave at the centre, the notch flanked by two rounded lobes; antennae 13–16-segmented. The Australian species S. seclusus is an exception, its soldiers being further divided into a medium form, so that they are trimorphic (major, medium and minor) (first reported by Miller 1987).
/genus/schedorhinotermes/.taxonomy_note: Schedorhinotermes maximus, mentioned in the original book, was removed by Krishna in 1970 on Emerson's advice and established in the separate genus Macrorhinotermes.

/genus/sinocapritermes/.alate: Alate head capsule rather densely hairy, the frontal gland pore small, narrow and long, oval. Postclypeus less than half as long as wide, with a median suture at the centre. The distance between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth of the right mandible is slightly greater than that between the first and second marginal teeth. Antennae 15-segmented, tibial spur formula likewise 2:2:2.
/genus/sinocapritermes/.biology: Species of the genus generally nest underground or live in fallen logs and tree holes; their food includes humus, grass roots and decayed wood, and they are a common kind of termite in subtropical woodlands. Thirteen species are known in the genus, mostly distributed in warm, humid low hills.
/genus/sinocapritermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account of Sinocapritermes in the original book, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/sinocapritermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head rectangular and without a frontal ridge, the middle of the left mandible twisted, its apex hooked and swollen behind the hook, the right mandible knife-like; labrum narrow and long, its anterior margin concave; antennae 14-segmented, tibial spur formula 2:2:2; the frontal gland pore of the alate small and narrow.
/genus/sinocapritermes/.distribution: Oriental region of southern China; the known records are concentrated in Guangxi, Yunnan, Hainan, Guangdong, Sichuan and other provinces and regions, extending northwards along the coasts of Fujian and Zhejiang, with the Tianmu Mountains as its northern limit.
/genus/sinocapritermes/.soldier: The hairs on the soldier head capsule are of medium density to fairly dense; the head is rectangular and the frons without a ridge. Mandibles asymmetrical: the middle of the left mandible is moderately twisted, the apex curved into a hook, swollen behind the hook; the right mandible is sword-like, slightly curved at the apex. Antennae 14-segmented. Labrum long and narrow, its anterior margin concave, the anterolateral corners slightly projecting outwards. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

/genus/sinonasutitermes/.alate: Alate head and pronotum densely covered with soft hairs mixed with a few long hairs, the long hairs on the periphery of the pronotum more numerous than those on the head. Head nearly circular, fontanelle oval and with an apical fork; compound eyes oval, large and projecting; ocelli oval, projecting outwards; postclypeus convex, three to four times as wide as long. The apical tooth of the left mandible is larger than the first marginal tooth, the cutting edge between the two teeth straight, and the second marginal tooth is reduced and merged with the posterior cutting edge of the first marginal tooth; the second marginal tooth of the right mandible is close to the first, and the mandibular file bears 8–9 striae. Antennae 15-segmented. Pronotum slightly arched near the middle of the anterior margin. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/sinonasutitermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account of Sinonasutitermes in the original book, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/sinonasutitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier dimorphic (trimorphic in a few species), body yellow; head broadly circular and broader than long, the posterior margin broadly rounded; nasus yellow tinged with brown; the sharp teeth of the mandibles very small; antennae 13-segmented in the major soldier and 12-segmented in the minor; pronotum saddle-shaped with its anterior half upright; tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/sinonasutitermes/.distribution: Oriental region; distributed in southern China, found in subtropical evergreen broad-leaved forest areas.
/genus/sinonasutitermes/.soldier: Soldier in two forms, major and minor, the body yellow and the nasus yellow tinged with brown. Head and thorax almost without hairs, the tip of the nasus bearing a few hairs, and the abdominal tergites with a few additional fine short hairs. The major soldier has a head broader than long, broadly circular, the sides rounded and convex, the posterior margin broadly rounded; antennae 13-segmented, the third segment twice as long as the second or longer; the sharp teeth of the mandibles are very small. Pronotum saddle-shaped, its anterior half upright. The minor soldier resembles the major in colour, pilosity and head shape; the sharp teeth of the mandibles are very small, mostly dot-like; antennae 12-segmented. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2 in both forms, tarsi 4-segmented. In a few species (S. admirabilis and S. trimorphus) a medium soldier is further distinguished, so that the soldiers are trimorphic (major, medium and minor).

/genus/speculitermes/.alate: Alate head densely hairy, oval, broader than long. Fontanelle large, oval. Compound eyes large, nearly circular and projecting; ocelli small, oval. The apical tooth of the mandibles is distinctly larger than the first marginal tooth, and the third marginal tooth of the left mandible meets the first marginal tooth at an angle. Antennae 15-segmented. Pronotum about as broad as the head capsule, or slightly narrower than the head. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/speculitermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account of Speculitermes in the original book, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/speculitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head nearly rectangular, the lateral margins slightly parallel; mandibles stout, broad at the base, each with a distinct tooth at the middle of the inner margin; antennae 14-segmented; pronotum saddle-shaped, tarsi 4-segmented, cerci 2-segmented.
/genus/speculitermes/.distribution: Its range spans two major zoogeographical realms, the Neotropical and the Oriental.
/genus/speculitermes/.soldier: Soldier mandibles dark brown, the head yellowish brown, the labrum and antennae pale yellow, the pronotum dull yellow; long and short hairs are intermingled on the anterior half of the head. The outline of the head is nearly rectangular, the lateral margins roughly parallel. Labrum ligulate, broader than long. Mandibles strong, broad at the base, curved inwards at the apex, each with a distinct tooth at the middle of the inner margin. Postmentum long, the waist distinct. Antennae 14-segmented. Pronotum saddle-shaped. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.

/genus/stylotermes/.alate: Alate body length (excluding wings) usually less than that of the soldier. Fontanelle very small; postclypeus varying in the degree of its protrusion. On the left mandible the first marginal tooth is larger than the second. Antennae with 18–22 segments. Pronotum flat, narrower than the head capsule. Forewing scale larger than the hindwing scale; wing membrane bare, without setae; venation reticulate. Femur not swollen; tibial spur formula 3:2:2; tarsi with three tarsomeres. Cerci with two segments, and without styli.
/genus/stylotermes/.biology: A rather distinctive group, mostly entering the xylem through wounds in the trunk and damaging living trees; sap often exudes from the attacked sites, and in severe cases dark brown sludge-like faecal material accumulates on the outside. Colonies are small to medium in size. In China recorded from Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Guangdong, Hainan and Fujian, with 34 species known; abroad, about ten species in India and Bangladesh and one in Malaysia.
/genus/stylotermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account in the original book's section on Stylotermes, rearranged and rewritten)
/genus/stylotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head capsule rectangular; labrum semicircular and lacking a hyaline tip; mandibles sabre-shaped, stout and strong, each with one or two small blunt teeth on the inner edge below the middle; tarsi with three tarsomeres, tibial spur formula 3:2:2, cerci with two segments.
/genus/stylotermes/.distribution: Oriental Region; mainly in the provinces from south-western to southern China; outside China recorded from India, Bangladesh and Malaysia.
/genus/stylotermes/.soldier: Soldier head capsule mostly rectangular, rarely oval-rectangular; fontanelle either small or raised. Labrum semicircular, without a hyaline tip, its apex projecting or straight, its surface bearing more than ten setae. Mandibles sabre-shaped, stout and strong, each with one or two small blunt teeth on the inner edge below the middle. Antennae with 13–19 segments. Compound eyes reduced to dots; ocelli small or absent. Postmentum club-shaped, narrowed at the waist. Pronotum flat, narrower than the head capsule. Femur swollen; tibial spur formula 3:2:2; tarsi with three tarsomeres. Without styli; cerci with two segments.
/genus/stylotermes/.taxonomy_note: Because the tarsi have only three tarsomeres, some authors have proposed treating this genus as a separate family, Stylotermitidae.

/genus/xiaitermes/.book_ref: (the genus-level account in the original book's section on Xiaitermes, rearranged and rewritten)
/genus/xiaitermes/.diagnosis: Soldiers of two sizes, major and minor; head broadly rounded, wider than long; nasus tubular, its apex slightly upturned; a small tubercle on each side at the base of the nasus; not constricted behind the antennal sockets; apical teeth of the mandibles blunt and indistinct; anterior margin of the pronotum obliquely upturned; antennae with 13–14 segments.
/genus/xiaitermes/.distribution: Oriental Region; recorded from Zhejiang and other subtropical areas of China, mostly in low hills and uplands.
/genus/xiaitermes/.soldier: Soldiers of two sizes, major and minor. Head capsule almost bare, the tip of the nasus with only a few short setae. Head broadly rounded, wider than long; nasus tubular, its apex slightly upturned in lateral view; a small tubercle on each side at the base of the nasus. Not constricted behind the antennal sockets; antennae with 13–14 segments. Apical teeth of the mandibles blunt-angled or indistinct. Anterior margin of the pronotum obliquely upturned, concave at the middle, the posterior margin broad and rather flat. Hind tibia rather short; tibial spur formula 2:2:2; tarsi with four tarsomeres.
/genus/xiaitermes/.taxonomy_note: The key to species in the original book records two species: X. yinxianensis and X. tiantaiensis. Ye et al. 2026 (Insects 17(6):602), on mitochondrial genome and morphological evidence, synonymised X. tiantaiensis under X. yinxianensis (junior synonym), so the genus is now monotypic; the "soldier monotype" attributed to tiantaiensis is in fact the minor soldier morph of yinxianensis.
/genus/xiaitermes/.worker: Workers of two sizes, major and minor. Head with sparse setae, its outline broad and rounded, widest behind the antennal sockets; fontanelle a circular pit, situated immediately behind the intersection of the T-shaped suture; postclypeus raised. Antennae with 14–15 segments. Pronotum broad, concave at the middle of its anterior margin. Hind tibia rather short.
